Section 7 re-defines 'exposed' via escape probability, equivalent to Definition 1.2's harmonic-measure version; kept as its own definition instead of an also_stated_at copy because the wording and criterion differ.

nodes.name: Integer ranges and natural numbers
nodes.statement: For an integer $i$, we denote $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq i} = \{i, i+1, \dots\}$ and $\mathbb{N} = \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ in particular.

nodes.name: Law of random walk from x
nodes.statement: For $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, we denote the distribution of random walk $(S_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ from $S_0 = x$ by $\mathbb{P}_x$.

nodes.name: Random walk (simple symmetric)
nodes.statement: Here and throughout, ``random walk'' refers to simple, symmetric random walk in $\mathbb{Z}^d$.

nodes.name: Return time to a set
nodes.statement: We denote the first time that random walk returns to a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ by $\tau_A = \inf\{j \geq 1: S_j \in A\}$.

nodes.name: Harmonic measure
Equation (1.1)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{H}_A (y) = \lim_{\| x \| \to \infty} \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A} = y \mid \tau_A < \infty ).
nodes.label: lim him

nodes.name: Existence of the harmonic measure limit
nodes.statement: This limit exists and does not depend on the sequence in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ that is implicit in the notation ``$\|x\| \to \infty$,'' so $\mathbb{H}_A$ is well defined (see, e.g., \cite[Chapter 2]{lawler2013intersections}).
conclusions: This limit exists and does not depend on the sequence in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ that is implicit in the notation

nodes.name: Configurations (state space of HAT)
nodes.statement: The state space of HAT is $\mathrm{Conf}_d = \{V \subset \mathbb{Z}^d: 2 \leq |V| < \infty \}$, the collection of $d$-dimensional {\em configurations}, or finite subsets of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with at least two elements.

nodes.name: HAT configuration at time t
nodes.statement: We denote the HAT configuration at time $t \in \mathbb{N}$ by $U_t$.

nodes.name: Sites of activation and transport
nodes.statement:
To obtain $U_{t+1}$ from $U_t$, we first remove an element $X_t$ from $U_t$ according to $\mathbb{H}_{U_t}$. Then, we consider a random walk from $X_t$ that is conditioned to hit $U_t {\setminus} \{X_t\}$. If this random walk steps from $Y_t$ when it first does so, then we add $Y_t$ to form
\[
U_{t+1} = (U_t \setminus \{X_t\}) \cup \{Y_t\}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: One HAT step removes $X_t$ by harmonic measure and adds $Y_t$, the site from which a walk from $X_t$ conditioned to hit the rest first steps into it.

nodes.name: HAT transition kernel p_U(x,y)
nodes.statement:
In other words, given $U_t$, the probability that activation occurs at $x$ and transport occurs to $y$ is
\begin{equation} p_{U_t} (x,y) = \mathbb{H}_{U_t} (x) \, \mathbb{P}_x ( S_{\tau - 1} = y \mid \tau < \infty ),
\end{equation}
where $\tau$ abbreviates $\tau_{U_t {\setminus} \{x\}}$.

nodes.name: Equation (1.2)
nodes.statement: p_{U_t} (x,y) = \mathbb{H}_{U_t} (x) \, \mathbb{P}_x ( S_{\tau - 1} = y \mid \tau < \infty ),
nodes.label: eq tps0

nodes.name: Activation and transport components
nodes.statement: We refer to the two factors in \eqref{eq tps0} as the activation and transport components of the dynamics.

nodes.name: Harmonic activation and transport (HAT)
nodes.statement: HAT is the discrete-time Markov chain $(U_t)_{t \geq 0}$ on the state space $\mathrm{Conf}_d$ with transition probabilities given by \begin{equation} \mathbf{P} \left( U_{t+1} = (U_t \setminus \{x\}) \cup \{y\} \bigm\vert U_t \right) = \begin{cases} p_{U_t} (x,y) & x \neq y,\\ \sum_{z \in \mathbb{Z}^d} p_{U_t} (z,z) & x = y, \end{cases} \end{equation} for $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}^d$.
nodes.statement_short: HAT: Markov chain on finite configurations that removes an element by harmonic measure and re-adds it where a conditioned random walk last stepped.
nodes.genus: discrete-time Markov chain $(U_t)_{t \geq 0}$ on the state space $\mathrm{Conf}_d$

nodes.name: Equation (1.3)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{P} \left( U_{t+1} = (U_t \setminus \{x\}) \cup \{y\} \bigm\vert U_t \right) = \begin{cases} p_{U_t} (x,y) & x \neq y,\\ \sum_{z \in \mathbb{Z}^d} p_{U_t} (z,z) & x = y, \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq tps

nodes.name: Diameter and law of HAT
nodes.statement: To state them, we denote the diameter of $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ by $\mathrm{diam} (A) = \sup_{x,y \in A} \|x-y\|$ and the law of HAT from $V$ (i.e., conditioned on $U_0 = V$) by $\mathbf{P}_V$.

nodes.name: Conservation of mass
nodes.statement: {\em Conservation of mass}. The number of elements in $U_t$ is fixed by the initial configuration $U_0$. Consequently, every irreducible component of the state space is contained in $\mathrm{Conf}_{d,n} = \{V \subset \mathbb{Z}^d: |V| = n\}$ for some $n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2}$.
conclusions: The number of elements in $U_t$ is fixed by the initial configuration $U_0$
every irreducible component of the state space is contained in $\mathrm{Conf}_{d,n} = \{V \subset \mathbb{Z}^d: |V| = n\}$ for some $n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2}$

nodes.name: Variable connectivity
nodes.statement: {\em Variable connectivity}. If $|U_0| \geq 3$, then $U_t$ eventually reaches a configuration with two or more connected components.
conclusions: $U_t$ eventually reaches a configuration with two or more connected components

nodes.name: Asymmetric behavior of diameter
nodes.statement:
{\em Asymmetric behavior of diameter}. The diameter of $U_t$ increases by at most one with each step: for every configuration $V$,
\begin{equation} \mathbf{P}_V (\mathrm{diam} (U_{t+1}) \leq \mathrm{diam} (U_t) + 1) = 1.
\end{equation}
In contrast, the diameter of $U_t$ can decrease by as much as $\mathrm{diam} (U_t) - 1$ in one step. For example, if $|V| = 2$, then $\mathbf{P}_V (\mathrm{diam} (U_1) = 1) = 1$.
conclusions: The diameter of $U_t$ increases by at most one with each step
the diameter of $U_t$ can decrease by as much as $\mathrm{diam} (U_t) - 1$ in one step

nodes.name: Equation (1.4)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{P}_V (\mathrm{diam} (U_{t+1}) \leq \mathrm{diam} (U_t) + 1) = 1.
nodes.label: amlg0

nodes.name: Translation invariance
nodes.statement:
{\em Translation invariance}. The transition probabilities satisfy
\[
\mathbf{P}_{W} (U_1 = V) = \mathbf{P}_{W+x} (U_1 = V+x)
\] 
for all $V, W \in \mathrm{Conf}_d$ and $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$.

nodes.name: Translation equivalence class
nodes.statement:
This motivates the association of each set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ to the equivalence class $\widehat A$ consisting of the translates of $A$:
\[ \widehat A = \big\{ B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d: \exists x \in \mathbb{Z}^d: B = A + x \big\}.\]

nodes.name: Isolated and non-isolated configurations
nodes.statement: If $A \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ is finite and if $x \in A$, then we say that $x$ is exposed in $A$ if $\mathbb{H}_A (x) > 0$. We say that $A$ is isolated if every element that is exposed in $A$ has no neighbors in $A$; we say that $A$ is non-isolated if it is not isolated. We denote by $\mathrm{Iso}_{d,n}$ and $\mathrm{NonIso}_{d,n}$ the collections of isolated and non-isolated $n$-element configurations in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, respectively. We denote the collections of the corresponding equivalence classes of configurations by $\mathrm{\widehat{I}so}_{d,n}$ and $\mathrm{\widehat{N}onIso}_{d,n}$.
nodes.statement_short: A set is isolated if every element with positive harmonic measure has no neighbors in it; Iso/NonIso denote the corresponding configuration classes.

nodes.name: Positive recurrence for two or three elements
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that HAT is positive recurrent on $\mathrm{\widehat{N}onIso}_{d,n}$, for any dimension $d$, when the number of elements $n$ is two or three.
assumptions: when the number of elements $n$ is two or three

nodes.name: Argument for positive recurrence when n = 3
nodes.statement: When $n=3$, isolated elements are removed with uniformly positive probability, which prevents a configuration's diameter from steadily growing.
nodes.statement_short: Isolated elements are removed with uniformly positive probability, so the diameter cannot grow steadily.

nodes.name: Positive recurrence in two dimensions
nodes.statement: For every $n \geq 2$, from any $n$-element subset of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, HAT converges to a unique probability measure, supported on $\mathrm{\widehat{N}onIso}_{2,n}$. In particular, HAT is positive recurrent on $\mathrm{\widehat{N}onIso}_{2,n}$ for every $n \geq 2$.
conclusions: HAT converges to a unique probability measure, supported on $\mathrm{\widehat{N}onIso}_{2,n}$
HAT is positive recurrent on $\mathrm{\widehat{N}onIso}_{2,n}$ for every $n \geq 2$
also_stated_at: Nevertheless, it is possible to prove that, in two dimensions, HAT is positive recurrent on the class of non-isolated configurations for every $n \geq 2$.
nodes.label: pos rec

nodes.name: Collapse
nodes.statement: Informally, collapse occurs when the diameter of a configuration is reduced to its logarithm over a number of steps proportional to this logarithm.

nodes.name: Collapse occurs with high probability
nodes.statement: When a configuration has a sufficiently large diameter in terms of $n$, collapse occurs with high probability in $n$ \cite[Theorem 1.5]{calvert2021}.
assumptions: a configuration has a sufficiently large diameter in terms of $n$
conclusions: collapse occurs with high probability in $n$

nodes.name: Transience in high dimensions
nodes.statement: HAT is transient for every $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$.
nodes.label: trans

nodes.name: Isolated classes are transient
nodes.statement: It is unnecessary to qualify that HAT is transient on $\mathrm{\widehat{N}onIso}_{d,n}$, because the states of $\mathrm{\widehat{I}so}_{d,n}$ are transient for every $d$ and $n$.
conclusions: the states of $\mathrm{\widehat{I}so}_{d,n}$ are transient for every $d$ and $n$

nodes.name: Partition of a configuration
nodes.statement: By a partition $\mathcal{V}$ of a configuration $V$, we mean an ordered partition $(\mathcal{V}^1, \dots, \mathcal{V}^k)$ of $V$ into $k \geq 2$ nonempty, disjoint subsets.

nodes.name: Adding to and removing from a part
nodes.statement: For $i \in \{1,\dots,k\}$ and $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$, we denote by $\mathcal{V} \cup^i A$ and $\mathcal{V} \sd{i} A$ the partitions with $i$\textsuperscript{th} parts $\mathcal{V}^i \cup A$ and $\mathcal{V}^i \setminus A$, and all other parts equal to those of $\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: Part containing x
nodes.statement: If $x \in V$, then we denote the unique part of $V$ to which $x$ belongs by $[x]_{\mathcal{V}}$. In other words, $x \in \mathcal{V}^{[x]_{\mathcal{V}}}$.

nodes.name: Separation of a partition
nodes.statement:
The separation of a partition is the smallest distance between its parts:
\[
\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}) = \min_{1 \leq i \leq k} \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}^i, \mathcal{V}^{\neq i}).
\]
Here, we use $\mathrm{dist} (A,B) = \inf_{x \in A, y \in B} \|x-y\|$ to denote the distance between $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ and we use $\mathcal{V}^{\neq i}$ to denote the union $\cup_{j \neq i} \mathcal{V}^j$.

nodes.name: Natural partitioning
nodes.statement: Given a partition $\mathcal{V}$ of the time-$s$ configuration $U_s$, the natural partitioning $(\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq s}$ of $(U_t)_{t \geq s}$ with $\mathcal{V}$ is inductively defined by $\mathcal{U}_s = \mathcal{V}$ and \begin{equation} \mathcal{U}_{t+1} = \left( \mathcal{U}_t \sd{i_t} \{X_t\} \right) \cup^{i_t} \{Y_t\}, \quad t \geq s, \end{equation} in terms of the time-$t$ sites of activation $X_t$ and transport $Y_t$, and the part $i_t = [X_t]_{\mathcal{U}_t}$ of $\mathcal{U}_t$ to which $X_t$ belongs.
nodes.statement_short: Propagate a partition of $U_s$ forward in time by assigning each transported element to the part of the activated element.
nodes.label: nat part

nodes.name: Equation (1.5)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{U}_{t+1} = \left( \mathcal{U}_t \sd{i_t} \{X_t\} \right) \cup^{i_t} \{Y_t\}, \quad t \geq s,
nodes.label: c with u

nodes.name: Clustering; dimer, trimer, DOT clustering
nodes.statement: For $a, b > 0$, a partition $\mathcal{V} = (\mathcal{V}^1, \dots, \mathcal{V}^k)$ of a configuration $V$ is an $(a,b)$ clustering of $V$, denoted $\mathcal{V} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b} (V)$, if \begin{equation} |\mathcal{V}^i| \geq 2, \quad \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}^i, \mathcal{V}^{\neq i}) \geq a, \quad \text{and} \quad \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}^i) \leq b \log \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}^i, \mathcal{V}^{\neq i}), \quad 1 \leq i \leq k. \end{equation} We refer to the parts of a clustering as clusters. In particular, we call $\mathcal{V}^i$ a dimer if $|\mathcal{V}^i| = 2$ and a trimer if $|\mathcal{V}^i| = 3$. We say that $\mathcal{V}$ is an $(a,b)$ {\em dimer-or-timer} (DOT) clustering, denoted $\mathcal{V} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet (V)$, if $\mathcal{V}$ satisfies \begin{equation} |\mathcal{V}^i| \in \{2,3\}, \quad 1 \leq i \leq k, \end{equation} in addition to \eqref{abs rel sep}.
nodes.statement_short: An (a,b) clustering has parts of size at least 2, separation at least a and diameters at most b log(separation); DOT if all parts have 2 or 3 elements.
nodes.label: clustering def

nodes.name: Equation (1.6)
nodes.statement: |\mathcal{V}^i| \geq 2, \quad \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}^i, \mathcal{V}^{\neq i}) \geq a, \quad \text{and} \quad \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}^i) \leq b \log \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}^i, \mathcal{V}^{\neq i}), \quad 1 \leq i \leq k.
nodes.label: abs rel sep

nodes.name: Equation (1.7)
nodes.statement: |\mathcal{V}^i| \in \{2,3\}, \quad 1 \leq i \leq k,
nodes.label: two or three elems

nodes.name: Why dimers and trimers persist in d >= 5
nodes.statement: Dimers and trimers have a special status in $d \geq 5$ dimensions because they are the only clusters that can ``persist'' over many steps, in a sense that we elaborate at the end of the section. This is counterintuitive because smaller clusters are at greater risk of losing all of their elements to other clusters. However, in $d \geq 3$ dimensions, an activated element would likely escape to infinity in the absence of the conditioning in the transport component of the HAT dynamics \eqref{eq tps0}. Consequently, when clusters are well separated, the HAT dynamics biases the activated element to be transported to the cluster at which it was activated. As $d$ increases, this effect becomes more pronounced, enabling dimers and trimers to persist over many steps despite comprising few elements. In contrast, clusters of four or more elements cannot persist---not because they lose their elements to other, distant clusters---but because they can split into dimers or trimers, which grow apart as they persist.
nodes.statement_short: In high dimensions the conditioning in transport keeps elements in their own cluster, so small clusters persist while larger ones split.

nodes.name: Random-walk heuristic for the separation rate
nodes.statement: By viewing dimers and trimers at consecutive return times to a given orientation, we can model their individual motions as $d$-dimensional random walks (albeit not simple ones), which suggests that their separation grows at a rate of roughly $t^{1/2}$. These return times will be exponentially tight and so, because diameter increases at most linearly in time \eqref{amlg0}, the clusters' diameters should never exceed roughly $\log t$. These observations suggest that, after $t$ steps, the clusters should constitute a $(t^{1/2}, 1)$ DOT clustering of the HAT configuration. This is the heuristic behind our second main result.
nodes.statement_short: Viewed at return times, clusters move like random walks, so separation grows like $t^{1/2}$ while diameters stay $O(\log t)$.

nodes.name: The mechanism that produces transience
nodes.statement: Let $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$, and let $V \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}$. There exists $b = b(d,n) > 0$ such that, for any $\delta \in (0,\frac12)$, there exist $a = a(d,n,\delta) > 0$ and a $\mathbf{P}_V$-a.s.\@ finite random time $\theta = \theta (d,n,\delta) \in \mathbb{N}$ at which there is a clustering $\mathcal{W} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet (U_\theta)$ such that the natural partitioning $(\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq \theta}$ of $(U_t)_{t \geq \theta}$ with $\mathcal{W}$ satisfies \begin{equation} \mathcal{U}_t \in \mathrm{Clust}_{g(t-\theta),b}^\bullet (U_t), \quad t > \theta, \end{equation} where $g(s) = s^{\frac12 - \delta}$ for $s \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: For d>=5, n>=4, HAT a.s. eventually splits into dimers/trimers whose natural clustering separates at rate $t^{1/2-\delta}$ forever.
conclusions: there exist $a = a(d,n,\delta) > 0$ and a $\mathbf{P}_V$-a.s.\@ finite random time $\theta = \theta (d,n,\delta) \in \mathbb{N}$ at which there is a clustering $\mathcal{W} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet (U_\theta)$ such that the natural partitioning $(\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq \theta}$ of $(U_t)_{t \geq \theta}$ with $\mathcal{W}$ satisfies \begin{equation} \mathcal{U}_t \in \mathrm{Clust}_{g(t-\theta),b}^\bullet (U_t), \quad t > \theta, \end{equation} where $g(s) = s^{\frac12 - \delta}$ for $s \geq 0$.
nodes.label: fate

nodes.name: Equation (1.8)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{U}_t \in \mathrm{Clust}_{g(t-\theta),b}^\bullet (U_t), \quad t > \theta,
nodes.label: dot conds

nodes.name: Interpretation of Theorem 3
nodes.statement:
Theorem \ref{fate} identifies an a.s.\ finite random time $\theta$ at which there is a clustering of $U_\theta$ into dimers or trimers and forever after which {\em the same dimers or trimers} become steadily, increasingly separated---in terms both absolute and relative to their diameters. In particular, \eqref{dot conds} is stronger than 
\[
\mathrm{Clust}_{g (t-\theta),b}^\bullet (U_t) \neq \emptyset, \quad t > \theta,
\]
because it rules--out the exchange of elements between clusters after time $\theta$. 
According to the preceding heuristic (which the proof makes precise), a growth rate of $s^{\frac12}$ would be tight.

nodes.name: Irreducibility
nodes.statement: HAT is irreducible on $\mathrm{\widehat{N}onIso}_{d,n}$, for every $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 2$.
nodes.label: irred

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$, and let $V$ be the $n$-element segment $\{(j,0,\dots,0): 1 \leq j \leq n\} \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$. It suffices to show that $\widehat V$ is transient, since $\widehat V \in \mathrm{\widehat{N}onIso}_{d,n}$ and since HAT is irreducible on $\mathrm{\widehat{N}onIso}_{d,n}$ by Theorem~\ref{irred}. Theorem~\ref{fate} implies that there is a $\mathbf{P}_V$-a.s.\@ finite time $\theta$ such that $\mathrm{diam} (U_t) \geq n$ for $t \geq \theta$. Because $\mathrm{diam} (\widehat V) = n - 1 < n$, this implies that there are $\mathbf{P}_V$-a.s.\ finitely many returns to $\widehat V$, hence $\widehat V$ is transient.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce via irreducibility (Theorem 4) to transience of the segment class; Theorem 3 forces diameter >= n eventually, so finitely many returns.

nodes.name: Reference dimers and trimers
nodes.statement:
Specifically, we define $\mathrm{Ref}$ to be the collection of reference dimers and trimers
\[
\mathrm{Ref} = \left\{ \{x,x+e_1\}: x \in \mathbb{Z}^d\right\} \cup \left\{\{x, x+e_1, x+2e_1\}: x \in \mathbb{Z}^d\right\}
\]
and denote the collection of tuples of such configurations by $\mathrm{Ref}^\times$.

\]

nodes.name: Formation of dimers and trimers
nodes.statement: Fix $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$. For every $a > 0$, there exist $N = N (a,d,n) \in \mathbb{N}$ and $p = p(a,d,n) \in (0,1]$ such that, for any $V \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}$, \begin{equation} \mathbf{P}_{V} \left( \mathrm{Clust}_{a,1}^\bullet (U_N) \cap \mathrm{Ref}^\times \neq \emptyset \right) \geq p. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: From any configuration, HAT reaches one with an (a,1) DOT clustering of reference segments within N steps with probability at least p, both independent of the diameter.
nodes.label: thm form dot

nodes.name: Equation (1.9)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{P}_{V} \left( \mathrm{Clust}_{a,1}^\bullet (U_N) \cap \mathrm{Ref}^\times \neq \emptyset \right) \geq p.
nodes.label: thm eq form dot

nodes.name: Heuristic: d = 5 is the critical dimension
nodes.statement:
Consider a pair of dimers. Until they exchange elements, we can model the distance between them by the norm of a $d$-dimensional random walk. If they never exchange elements, then, because random walk is transient in $d \geq 3$ dimensions, their separation will grow steadily and without bound, as Theorem \ref{fate} predicts.

This basic picture is modified by the fact that dimers exchange elements over a number of steps which depends on their separation. Specifically, if the dimers are separated by a distance $a$, then they will typically exchange elements over $a^{d-2}$ steps. This timescale reflects the fact that a random walk from the origin $o \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, which is conditioned to return to $\{o,x\}$ for $o \neq x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, reaches $x$ first with a probability of roughly $\|x\|^{2-d}$. If the dimers do not exchange elements during a period of $a^2$ steps, then the separation of the dimers typically doubles over the same period, after which it takes $2^{d-2}$ times longer for them to exchange elements. Hence, if $d \geq 5$, then dimer separation grows quickly enough that elements are never exchanged, which suggests transience. In contrast, if $d \in \{3,4\}$, then dimers typically consolidate before their separation doubles, which suggests recurrence. An analogous heuristic concludes the same of trimers.
nodes.statement_short: Dimers a apart exchange elements after ~a^{d-2} steps while separation doubles in a^2 steps, so exchanges stop when d>=5 but not in d in {3,4}.
nodes.section: A heuristic which suggests that $d=5$ is the critical dimension for transience

nodes.name: Origin and standard basis vectors
nodes.statement: We use $o$ to denote the origin in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $e_j$ to denote the element of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $j$\textsuperscript{th} coordinate equal to $1$ and all other coordinates equal to $0$.

nodes.name: Integer part
nodes.statement: For a real number $r$, we use $[r]$ to denote the integer part of $r$.

nodes.name: Exterior vertex boundary and radius
nodes.statement: We use $\partial A$ to denote the exterior vertex boundary $\{z \in \mathbb{Z}^d: \mathrm{dist}(z,A) = 1\}$ of a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$, and $\mathrm{rad} (A) = \{\|x\| : x \in A\}$ to denote its radius.

nodes.name: Expectations and indicators
nodes.statement: We use $\mathbb{E}_x$ and $\mathbf{E}_V$ to denote expectation with respect to $\mathbb{P}_x$ and $\mathbf{P}_V$, and $\mathbf{1}_E$ to denote the indicator of an event $E$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic notation
nodes.statement: We use $f \lesssim g$ to denote the estimate $f \leq c g$ for a constant $c$ that may depend on $d$, and we denote such a quantity $f$ by $O(g)$.

nodes.name: n-dependent asymptotic notation
nodes.statement: In some instances, we use $f \lesssim_n g$ to denote the same estimate, except permitting $c$ to depend on $n$ as well.

nodes.name: Reverse asymptotic notation
nodes.statement: We use $f \gtrsim g$ and $\Omega (g)$ analogously, for the reverse estimate.

nodes.name: Comparable quantities
nodes.statement: We use $f \asymp g$ when $f \lesssim g$ and $f \gtrsim g$.

nodes.name: Uniformly positive probability of persistent DOT separation
nodes.statement: Fix $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$. There exists $b = b (n) \geq 1$ such that, for any $\delta \in (0,\frac12)$, there exists $\alpha = \alpha (d,n,\delta) > 0$ such that, if $W \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}$ has a clustering $\mathcal{W} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{\alpha,b}^\bullet (W) \cap \mathrm{Ref}^\times$, then \begin{equation} \mathbf{P}_{W} (\xi = \infty) \geq \frac14, \end{equation} where $\xi$ is the first time that the natural clustering $(\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ of $(U_t)_{t \geq 0}$ with $\mathcal{W}$ is not in $\mathrm{Clust}_{g(t),b}^\bullet (U_t)$ where $g(s) = s^{\frac12 - \delta}$ for $s \geq 0$, i.e., \[ \xi = \inf \{t \geq 0: \mathcal{U}_t \notin \mathrm{Clust}_{g(t),b}^\bullet (U_t)\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: A well-separated reference DOT clustering keeps separating at rate $t^{1/2-\delta}$ forever with probability at least 1/4.
nodes.label: inf xi

nodes.name: Equation (2.1)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{P}_{W} (\xi = \infty) \geq \frac14,
nodes.label: eq inf xi

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Fix $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$. Let $\alpha > 0$ and $b \geq 1$ be the constants from Proposition~\ref{inf xi}. Fix $\delta \in (0,\frac12)$. In these terms, denote $g(s) = s^{\frac12-\delta}$ for $s \geq 0$. Additionally, let $\psi$ be a function which, given a configuration $U \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}$ that has a clustering in $\mathrm{Clust}_{\alpha,b}^\bullet (U)$, determines one such clustering. (We use $\psi$ to ``pick'' one of potentially multiple clusterings; it is otherwise unimportant.) We define $\theta$ in terms of two sequences of random times, $(\tau_i)_{i \geq 1}$ and $(\xi_i)_{i \geq 0}$. In words, $\tau_i$ is the first time $t \geq \xi_{i-1}$ at which $U_t$ has an $(\alpha,b)$ DOT clustering in $\mathrm{Ref}^\times$, and $\xi_i$ is the first time $t > \tau_i$ at which the natural clustering $(\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq \tau_i}$ of $(U_t)_{t \geq \tau_i}$ with $\psi (U_{\tau_i})$ is not a $(g(t-\tau_i),b)$ DOT clustering of $U_t$. More precisely, we define $\xi_0 = 0$ and, for $i \geq 1$, \begin{align*} \tau_i &= \inf \left\{t \geq \xi_{i-1}: \mathrm{Clust}_{\alpha,b}^\bullet (U_t) \cap \mathrm{Ref}^\times \neq \emptyset \right\}, \quad \text{and}\\ \xi_i &= \inf \left\{t > \tau_i: \mathcal{U}_t \notin \mathrm{Clust}_{ g(t-\tau_i),b}^\bullet (U_{t}) \right\}. \end{align*} Lastly, we define $\theta = \tau_I$ for $I = \inf \{i \geq 1: \tau_i < \infty, \xi_i = \infty\}$. By the definition of $\theta$, \eqref{dot conds} is satisfied, so it remains to show that $\theta$ is $\mathbf{P}_V$-a.s.\@ finite for every $V \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}$. Let $J =\inf \{j : \xi_j = \infty\}$. For every $V \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}$, we have \begin{equation} \mathbf{P}_V (\theta < \infty) = \mathbf{P}_V (I < \infty) = \mathbf{P}_V (J < \infty). \end{equation} The first equality follows from the definitions of $I$ and $\theta$. The second equality follows from the fact that $\mathbf{P}_V (\tau_i < \infty \mid \xi_{i-1} < \infty) = 1$, which is a simple consequence of Theorem~\ref{thm form dot}. To bound the tail probabilities of $J$, we write \begin{equation} \mathbf{P}_V (J > j+1 \,|\, J > j) = \frac{\mathbf{E}_V \big[ \mathbf{P}_{U_{\tau_j}} (\xi_1 < \infty); J > j\big]}{\mathbf{P}_V (J > j)} \leq \frac{3}{4}. \end{equation} The equality follows from the strong Markov property applied at time $\xi_j$ and the fact that $\mathbf{P}_{U_{\xi_j}} (\tau_1 < \infty) = 1$. The inequality is due to Proposition~\ref{inf xi}, which implies that $\mathbf{P}_{U_{\tau_j}} (\xi_1 < \infty)$ is at most $\frac34$. The bound \eqref{jj2} implies that $\mathbf{P}_V (J > j)$ is summable, so the Borel-Cantelli lemma implies that $J$ is $\mathbf{P}_V$-a.s.\@ finite, which by \eqref{thetatoj} implies the same of $\theta$.
nodes.statement_short: Define theta as the first success in a sequence of trials; Theorem 5 restarts trials a.s., Proposition 2.1 gives success probability >= 1/4, Borel-Cantelli concludes.

nodes.name: Escape probability
nodes.statement:
Define the escape probability of a finite set $A \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ by
\[
\mathrm{esc}_A (x) = \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A = \infty) \ \mathbf{1} (x \in A), \quad x \in \mathbb{Z}^d.
\]

nodes.name: Capacity
nodes.statement:
Further define the capacity of $A$ by
\[
\mathrm{cap}_A = \sum_{x \in A} \mathrm{esc}_A (x).
\]

nodes.name: Harmonic measure as normalized escape probability
Heuristic comparison of activation components
nodes.statement:
Consider a configuration $U \in \mathrm{Conf}_d$ that can be partitioned into $\mathcal{P} = (\mathcal{P}^1, \mathcal{P}^2)$ such that $|\mathcal{P}^1| \in \{2,3\}$ and $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P}) \geq a$ for some $a > 1$. We think of $\mathcal{P}^1$ as one DOT and $\mathcal{P}^2$ as the union of one or more clusters. If $x \in \mathcal{P}^1$, then we can bound below $\mathbb{H}_U (x)$ in terms of $\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{P}^1} (x)$, by noting that
\[
\mathrm{esc}_U (x) \geq \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{P}^1} (x) - \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\mathcal{P}^2} < \infty).
\]
In Section~\ref{hm bd}, we will prove that, if $a$ is at least a certain constant, then
\[
\mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{P}^1} (x) \gtrsim 1 \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\mathcal{P}^2} < \infty) \lesssim |U| a^{2-d}.
\]
The first bound is plausible because $\mathcal{P}^1$ only has two or three elements. The second bound follows from a union bound over the elements of $\mathcal{P}^2$ and the fact that, if $y \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ is sufficiently far from $x$, then $\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_y < \infty) \asymp \|x-y\|^{2-d}$.   
According to these bounds, the escape probability of $U$ satisfies
\[
\mathrm{esc}_U (x) \geq \left( 1 - O \left( |U| a^{2-d} \right) \right) \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{P}^1} (x).
\]
To convert this into a lower bound of $\mathbb{H}_U (x)$, we divide by the capacity of $U$ and identify a factor of $\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{P}^1} (x)$:
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb{H}_U (x) \geq \left( 1 - O \left( |U| a^{2-d} \right) \right) \frac{\mathrm{cap}_{\mathcal{P}^1}}{\mathrm{cap}_U} \mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{P}^1} (x).
\end{equation*}
Lastly, we note that the capacity of a union is at most the sum of the individual sets' capacities \cite[Proposition 2.2.1]{lawler2013intersections}, hence 
\begin{equation} \mathbb{H}_U (x) \geq \left( 1 - O \left( |U| a^{2-d} \right) \right) \frac{\mathrm{cap}_{\mathcal{P}^1}}{\mathrm{cap}_{\mathcal{P}^1} + \mathrm{cap}_{\mathcal{P}^2}} \mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{P}^1} (x).
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For a DOT far from the rest, HAT's harmonic measure is at least the DOT's own harmonic measure weighted by its share of the total capacity, up to 1-O(|U|a^{2-d}).

nodes.name: Equation (4.1)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{H}_U (x) \geq \left( 1 - O \left( |U| a^{2-d} \right) \right) \frac{\mathrm{cap}_{\mathcal{P}^1}}{\mathrm{cap}_{\mathcal{P}^1} + \mathrm{cap}_{\mathcal{P}^2}} \mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{P}^1} (x).
nodes.label: heur2

nodes.name: Finite sets and tuples of finite sets
nodes.statement:
Denote by $\mathrm{Fin}_d$ the collection of nonempty, finite subsets of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and by $\mathrm{Fin}_d^\times$ the collection of tuples of such sets, i.e., 
\[
\mathrm{Fin}_d = \{A \subset \mathbb{Z}^d: 1 \leq |A| < \infty\} \quad \text{and} \quad \mathrm{Fin}_d^\times = \cup_{k=1}^\infty \left\{ (\mathcal{A}^i)_{i=1}^k \in \mathrm{Fin}_d^k \right\}.
\]

nodes.name: Entries of a tuple
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{A} = (\mathcal{A}^i)_{i=1}^k \in \mathrm{Fin}_d^\times$, we refer to $\mathcal{A}^i$ as the $i$\textsuperscript{th} entry of $\mathcal{A}$ and we use $\# \mathcal{A}$ to denote the number of entries $k$ in $\mathcal{A}$.

nodes.name: Capacity and harmonic measure of a tuple of sets
nodes.statement:
We define the capacity of $\mathcal{A} \in \mathrm{Fin}_d^\times$ by
\[
\mathrm{cap}_{\mathcal{A}} = \sum_{i=1}^{\# \mathcal{A}} \mathrm{cap}_{\mathcal{A}^i},
\]
and the harmonic measure of $\mathcal{A}$ by 
\begin{equation} \mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{A}} (i,x) = \frac{\mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{A}^i} (x)}{\mathrm{cap}_{\mathcal{A}}}, \quad 1 \leq i \leq \# \mathcal{A}, \quad x \in \mathcal{A}^i.
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (4.2)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{A}} (i,x) = \frac{\mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{A}^i} (x)}{\mathrm{cap}_{\mathcal{A}}}, \quad 1 \leq i \leq \# \mathcal{A}, \quad x \in \mathcal{A}^i.

nodes.name: Heuristic comparison of transport components
nodes.statement:
Let $a > e$ and $b > 0$, and assume $d \geq 3$. Suppose that $U$ has an $(a,b)$ clustering $\mathcal{C} = (\mathcal{C}^1, \mathcal{C}^2)$, i.e., each cluster has at least two elements, the clusters are separated by a distance of at least $a$, and their diameters are at most $b \log \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{C}^1, \mathcal{C}^2)$. Fix elements $x \in \mathcal{C}^1$ and $y$ in the exterior vertex boundary of $\mathcal{C}^1 {\setminus} \{x\}$, and abbreviate $A = \mathcal{C}^1 {\setminus} \{x\}$. In these terms, we aim to compare the probability in \eqref{heur3} to
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A-1} = y \mid \tau_A < \infty).
\end{equation*}

For $\{S_{\tau-1} = y\}$ to occur, the random walk must visit $A$ before $\mathcal{C}^2$ because $y \in \partial A$ and $\mathrm{dist} (A, \mathcal{C}^2) > 1$ by assumption. Hence,   
\[
\mathbb{P}_x ( S_{\tau - 1} = y, \tau < \infty) = \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau - 1} = y, \tau_A < \tau_{\mathcal{C}^2}, \tau < \infty).
\]
In fact, because $\tau = \min \{\tau_A, \tau_{\mathcal{C}^2}\}$, this probability equals
\[
\mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A - 1} = y, \tau_A < \infty) - \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A - 1} = y, \tau_{\mathcal{C}^2} < \tau_A < \infty),
\]
which implies that
\begin{multline} \mathbb{P}_x ( S_{\tau - 1} = y \mid \tau < \infty) = \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A - 1} = y \mid \tau_A < \infty)\\ 
\times \underbrace{\frac{\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A < \infty)}{\mathbb{P}_x (\tau < \infty)}}_{( \ref{ict hat} \text{a})} \Bigg( 1 - \underbrace{\frac{\mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A - 1} = y, \tau_{\mathcal{C}^2} < \tau_A < \infty)}{\mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A - 1} = y, \tau_A < \infty)}}_{( \ref{ict hat} \text{b})} \Bigg).
\end{multline}


In Section~\ref{comp act}, we will show that (\ref{ict hat}a) and (\ref{ict hat}b) satisfy
\[
\text{(\ref{ict hat}a)} \geq 1 - O \left( |U| \left( b a^{-1} \log a\right)^{d-2} \right) \quad \text{and} \quad \text{(\ref{ict hat}b)} \leq O \left( |U| \left(b a^{-2} \log a \right)^{d-2} \right). 
\]
These bounds rely on the fact that random walk from $x$ hits a sufficiently distant set $B$ with a probability of at least $\mathrm{dist}(x,B)^{2-d}$ and at most $|B| \mathrm{dist}(x,B)^{2-d}$, up to constant factors. The separation properties that define an $(a,b)$ clustering are valuable for simplifying ratios of these quantities.

For example, the $O$ term in the lower bound of (\ref{ict hat}a) arises as the ratio of the hitting probabilities of $\mathcal{C}^2$ and $A$ from $x$. Since $\mathcal{C}^2$ and $A$ are distances of at least $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})$ and at most $\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{C}^1)$ from $x$, this ratio is roughly
\begin{equation*}
|U| \left( \frac{\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{C}^1)}{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})} \right)^{d-2} \leq |U| \left( \frac{b \log \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})}{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})} \right)^{d-2} \leq |U| \left( \frac{b \log a}{a} \right)^{d-2}.
\end{equation*}
The first inequality holds because $\mathcal{C}$ is $(\cdot, b)$ separated; the second holds because $\mathcal{C}$ is $(a,\cdot)$ separated and because $\frac{\log r}{r}$ decreases as $r > e$ increases.

The upper bound of (\ref{ict hat}b) follows from similar considerations, with the exception that the event in the numerator of (\ref{ict hat}b) requires random walk from $x$ to traverse a distance of $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})$ twice, from $\mathcal{C}^1$ to $\mathcal{C}^2$ and then back to $A$. This leads to an additional factor of $a^{2-d}$ in the bound of (\ref{ict hat}b).



Substituting these bounds into \eqref{ict hat} gives
\begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau-1} = y \mid \tau < \infty) \geq \left(1 - O \left( |U| \left( b a^{-1} \log a \right)^{d-2} \right) \right) \, \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A-1} = y \mid \tau_A < \infty).
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Transport in HAT agrees with intracluster transport up to a factor 1-O(|U|(b log a/a)^{d-2}) for an (a,b) clustering, via the decomposition (4.5).

nodes.name: Equation (4.5)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{P}_x ( S_{\tau - 1} = y \mid \tau < \infty) = \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A - 1} = y \mid \tau_A < \infty)\\ \times \underbrace{\frac{\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A < \infty)}{\mathbb{P}_x (\tau < \infty)}}_{( \ref{ict hat} \text{a})} \Bigg( 1 - \underbrace{\frac{\mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A - 1} = y, \tau_{\mathcal{C}^2} < \tau_A < \infty)}{\mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A - 1} = y, \tau_A < \infty)}}_{( \ref{ict hat} \text{b})} \Bigg).
nodes.label: ict hat

nodes.name: Equation (4.6)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau-1} = y \mid \tau < \infty) \geq \left(1 - O \left( |U| \left( b a^{-1} \log a \right)^{d-2} \right) \right) \, \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A-1} = y \mid \tau_A < \infty).
nodes.label: heur4

nodes.name: Tuples of configurations (state space of IHAT)
nodes.statement:
The state space of IHAT is the collection $\mathrm{Conf}_d^\times \subset \mathrm{Fin}_d^\times$ of tuples of configurations: 
\[
\mathrm{Conf}_d^\times = \cup_{k=1}^\infty \left\{ (\mathcal{A}^i)_{i=1}^k \in \mathrm{Conf}_d^k \right\}.
\]

nodes.name: IHAT state at time t
nodes.statement: We denote the state of IHAT at time $t \geq 0$ by $\mathcal{V}_t$.

nodes.name: IHAT transition kernel q
nodes.statement:
Given $\mathcal{V}_t$, we define the transition probabilities in terms of 
\begin{equation} q_{\mathcal{V}_t} (i,x,y) = \mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{V}_t} (i,x) \, \mathbb{P}_x ( S_{\tau-1} = y \mid \tau < \infty), \quad 1 \leq i \leq \# \mathcal{V}_t, \quad x, y \in \mathbb{Z}^d,
\end{equation}
where $\tau$ abbreviates $\tau_{\mathcal{V}_t^i \setminus \{x\}}$.

nodes.name: Equation (4.7)
nodes.statement: q_{\mathcal{V}_t} (i,x,y) = \mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{V}_t} (i,x) \, \mathbb{P}_x ( S_{\tau-1} = y \mid \tau < \infty), \quad 1 \leq i \leq \# \mathcal{V}_t, \quad x, y \in \mathbb{Z}^d,
nodes.label: eq tps q

nodes.name: Intracluster HAT (IHAT)
nodes.statement: IHAT is the discrete-time Markov chain $(\mathcal{V}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ on the state space $\mathrm{Conf}_d^\times$ with the following transition probabilities given by \begin{equation} \mathbf{Q} \left( \mathcal{V}_{t+1} = (\mathcal{V}_t \sd{i} \{x\}) \cup^i \{y\} \bigm\vert \mathcal{V}_t \right) = \begin{cases} q_{\mathcal{V}_t} (i,x,y) & x \neq y,\\ \sum_{j=1}^{\# \mathcal{V}_t} \sum_{z \in \mathbb{Z}^d} q_{\mathcal{V}_t} (j,z,z) & x = y, \end{cases} \end{equation} for $1 \leq i \leq \# \mathcal{V}_t$ and $x,y \in \mathbb{Z}^d$. We denote the law of IHAT from $\mathcal{V}$ by $\mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{V}}$.
nodes.statement_short: IHAT: Markov chain on tuples of configurations where activation uses the tuple harmonic measure and transport stays within the activated cluster.
nodes.genus: discrete-time Markov chain $(\mathcal{V}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ on the state space $\mathrm{Conf}_d^\times$

nodes.name: Equation (4.8)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{Q} \left( \mathcal{V}_{t+1} = (\mathcal{V}_t \sd{i} \{x\}) \cup^i \{y\} \bigm\vert \mathcal{V}_t \right) = \begin{cases} q_{\mathcal{V}_t} (i,x,y) & x \neq y,\\ \sum_{j=1}^{\# \mathcal{V}_t} \sum_{z \in \mathbb{Z}^d} q_{\mathcal{V}_t} (j,z,z) & x = y, \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq tps pprod

nodes.name: Green's function
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Equation (5.1)
nodes.statement: G(x) = \mathbb{E}_o \left[ \sum_{j=0}^\infty \mathbf{1} (S_j = x) \right], \quad x \in \mathbb{Z}^d.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: eq green

nodes.name: Green's function asymptotics
nodes.statement:
There is a constant $\kappa > e$ such that
\begin{equation} G(x) \asymp \|x\|^{2-d},
\end{equation}
for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ with norm $\|x\| \geq \kappa$ \cite[Theorem 4.3.1]{lawler2010random}.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.origin_citation: Lawler & Limic 2010, Random walk: a modern introduction (Theorem 4.3.1)

nodes.name: Equation (5.2)
nodes.statement: G(x) \asymp \|x\|^{2-d},
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: eq green asymp

nodes.name: Hitting probability bounds for a finite set
nodes.statement: Let $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ be nonempty and finite. If $\mathrm{dist} (x,A) \geq 1$, then \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A < \infty) \gtrsim \mathrm{dist} (x, A)^{2-d}. \end{equation} If $\mathrm{dist} (x, A) \geq \kappa$, then \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A < \infty) \lesssim |A| \mathrm{dist} (x,A)^{2-d}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Hitting probability of a finite set is at least dist^{2-d}, and at most |A| dist^{2-d} once dist exceeds $\kappa$.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
assumptions: Let $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ be nonempty and finite
nodes.label: simple set hit

nodes.name: Equation (5.3)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A < \infty) \gtrsim \mathrm{dist} (x, A)^{2-d}.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: eq simple set hit lb

nodes.name: Equation (5.4)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A < \infty) \lesssim |A| \mathrm{dist} (x,A)^{2-d}.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: eq simple set hit ub

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Suppose that $y_1$ is the element of $A$ closest to $x$ and that $z = y_2$ maximizes $\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_z < \infty)$ among $z \in A$. The inclusion $\{\tau_{y_1} < \infty\} \subseteq \{\tau_A < \infty\}$ and a union bound over the elements of $A$ imply that \[ \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{y_1} < \infty) \leq \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A < \infty) \leq |A| \, \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{y_2} < \infty). \] If $\mathrm{dist} (x,A) \in [1,\kappa)$, then \eqref{eq simple set hit lb} holds because $\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{y_1} < \infty) \gtrsim 1$. If $\mathrm{dist} (x,A) \geq \kappa$, then \eqref{eq simple set hit lb} holds because \[ \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{y_1} < \infty) = \frac{G(x-y_1)}{G(o)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq green asymp}}{\asymp} \|x-{y_1}\|^{2-d} = \mathrm{dist}(x,A)^{2-d}, \] while \eqref{eq simple set hit ub} holds because \[ \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{y_2} < \infty) = \frac{G(x-y_2)}{G(o)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq green asymp}}{\asymp} \|x-y_2\|^{2-d} \leq \mathrm{dist}(x,A)^{2-d}. \] The first equality in the two preceding displays is a standard identity; see, e.g., \cite[Equation 3.4]{popov2021}.
nodes.statement_short: Sandwich the hitting probability between the nearest point and a union bound, then use Green's function asymptotics.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Pick the nearest point and the most likely point of A
nodes.statement: Suppose that $y_1$ is the element of $A$ closest to $x$ and that $z = y_2$ maximizes $\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_z < \infty)$ among $z \in A$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick the nearest point and the most likely point of A
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Sandwich by single-point hitting and a union bound
nodes.statement:
The inclusion $\{\tau_{y_1} < \infty\} \subseteq \{\tau_A < \infty\}$ and a union bound over the elements of $A$ imply that
\[
\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{y_1} < \infty) \leq \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A < \infty) \leq |A| \, \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{y_2} < \infty).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Sandwich by single-point hitting and a union bound
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Case of bounded distance
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{dist} (x,A) \in [1,\kappa)$, then \eqref{eq simple set hit lb} holds because $\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{y_1} < \infty) \gtrsim 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Case of bounded distance
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Case of large distance via Green's function asymptotics
nodes.statement:
If $\mathrm{dist} (x,A) \geq \kappa$, then \eqref{eq simple set hit lb} holds because
\[
\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{y_1} < \infty) = \frac{G(x-y_1)}{G(o)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq green asymp}}{\asymp} \|x-{y_1}\|^{2-d} = \mathrm{dist}(x,A)^{2-d},
\]
while \eqref{eq simple set hit ub} holds because
\[
\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{y_2} < \infty) = \frac{G(x-y_2)}{G(o)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq green asymp}}{\asymp} \|x-y_2\|^{2-d} \leq \mathrm{dist}(x,A)^{2-d}.
\]
The first equality in the two preceding displays is a standard identity; see, e.g., \cite[Equation 3.4]{popov2021}.
nodes.statement_short: Case of large distance via Green's function asymptotics
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Coordinatewise partial order
nodes.statement:
The first property is that Green's function is nonincreasing with respect to a partial order $\preceq$ on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, defined for $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ by 
\[
x \preceq y \quad \iff \quad \forall i \in \llbracket d \rrbracket, \quad |x_i| \leq |y_i|,
\]
where $x_i$ and $y_i$ denote the $i$\textsuperscript{th} components of $x$ and $y$.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Monotonicity of Green's function in the coordinate partial order
nodes.statement: If $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and $x \preceq y$, then $G(x) \geq G(y)$.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: gpart

nodes.name: Green's function at the origin in dimension d
nodes.statement: To emphasize the dependence of this value on $d$, we denote it by $G_d (o)$.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Green's function at the origin is nonincreasing in dimension
nodes.statement: If $d_1 \leq d_2$, then $G_{d_1} (o) \geq G_{d_2} (o)$.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: g dec

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Montroll \cite[Eq. (2.10)]{montroll1956} expresses $G_d (o)$ in terms of $I_0$, the modified Bessel function of the first kind, as \[ G_d(o) = \int_0^\infty e^{-t} I_0 \Big( \frac{t}{d} \Big)^d d t.\] According to the integral representation of $I_0$ \cite[Eq. 9.6.19]{abramowitz1964}, $I_0 (\frac{t}{d})^d$ is the $L^{\frac{1}{d}}$ norm of $e^{t \cos \theta}$ with respect to the probability measure $\pi^{-1} d \theta$ on $[0,\pi]$: \[ I_0 \Big(\frac{t}{d}\Big)^d = \left(\frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^\pi e^{\tfrac{t \cos \theta}{d}} d \theta \right)^d.\] If $d_1 \leq d_2$, then the $L^{\frac{1}{d_2}}$ norm is no larger than the $L^{\frac{1}{d_1}}$ norm, hence \[ G_{d_1} (o) \geq \int_0^\infty e^{-t} I_0 \Big(\frac{t}{d_2}\Big)^{d_2} d t = G_{d_2} (o).\]
nodes.statement_short: Montroll's Bessel-function integral for G_d(o) and monotonicity of L^p norms in p.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Montroll's Bessel integral for G_d(o)
nodes.statement:
Montroll \cite[Eq. (2.10)]{montroll1956} expresses $G_d (o)$ in terms of $I_0$, the modified Bessel function of the first kind, as
\[ G_d(o) = \int_0^\infty e^{-t} I_0 \Big( \frac{t}{d} \Big)^d d t.\]
nodes.statement_short: Montroll's Bessel integral for G_d(o)
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Recognize the integrand as an L^{1/d} norm
nodes.statement:
According to the integral representation of $I_0$ \cite[Eq. 9.6.19]{abramowitz1964}, $I_0 (\frac{t}{d})^d$ is the $L^{\frac{1}{d}}$ norm of $e^{t \cos \theta}$ with respect to the probability measure $\pi^{-1} d \theta$ on $[0,\pi]$:
\[ I_0 \Big(\frac{t}{d}\Big)^d = \left(\frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^\pi e^{\tfrac{t \cos \theta}{d}} d \theta \right)^d.\]
nodes.statement_short: Recognize the integrand as an L^{1/d} norm
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Monotonicity of L^p norms concludes
nodes.statement:
If $d_1 \leq d_2$, then the $L^{\frac{1}{d_2}}$ norm is no larger than the $L^{\frac{1}{d_1}}$ norm, hence
\[ G_{d_1} (o) \geq \int_0^\infty e^{-t} I_0 \Big(\frac{t}{d_2}\Big)^{d_2} d t = G_{d_2} (o).\]
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of L^p norms concludes
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Proof of the bound G_d(o) <= 5/4
nodes.statement: Note that $G_d (o) = (1-p_d)^{-1}$, where $p_d$ is the probability that $d$-dimensional random walk from the origin returns to the origin \cite[Equation 3.15]{popov2021}. Since $p_4 \leq 0.2$ \cite{finch2003}, Lemma~\ref{g dec} implies a bound of $G_d (o) \leq \frac54$ when $d \geq 4$.
nodes.statement_short: Express G_d(o) via the return probability p_d, use p_4 <= 0.2 and monotonicity in d (Lemma 5.3).
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Bound on G_d(o) for d >= 4
nodes.statement: If $d \geq 4$, then $G_d (o) \leq \frac54$.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: g5

nodes.name: Escape probability and harmonic measure lower bounds for sets of at most four elements
nodes.statement: Let $d \geq 4$. If $U \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ has $|U| \leq 4$, then \begin{equation} \mathrm{esc}_U (x) \geq \frac{4 - 3 G(o)}{G(o)} \geq \frac15 \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{H}_U (x) \geq \frac{1}{16}, \quad x \in U. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: min es

nodes.name: Equation (5.5)
nodes.statement: \mathrm{esc}_U (x) \geq \frac{4 - 3 G(o)}{G(o)} \geq \frac15 \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{H}_U (x) \geq \frac{1}{16}, \quad x \in U.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: eq min es2

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $x \in U$. We can express $\mathrm{esc}_U (x)$ in terms of $N = \sum_{j=1}^\infty \mathbf{1} (S_j \in U)$, the number of returns made to $U$ by random walk, as \begin{equation} \mathrm{esc}_U (x) = \mathbb{P}_x (N=0) = 1 - \frac{\mathbb{E}_x [N]}{\mathbb{E}_x [N \mid N > 0]}. \end{equation} To bound above $\mathbb{E}_x [N]$, we note that \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}_x [N] = \sum_{y \in U} G(x-y) - 1. \end{equation} Since $x \in U$ and $|U| \leq 4$, there are $u, v, w\in \mathbb{Z}^d$ such that \[ \{x - y: y \in U\} \subseteq \{o, u, v, w\} \quad \text{and} \quad \exists k,l, m \in \{1,\dots,d\}: u \succeq e_k, \,\, v \succeq e_l, \,\, w \succeq e_m. \] Green's function is nonnegative and nonincreasing in $\succeq$ (Lemma \ref{gpart}), hence \begin{equation*} \sum_{y \in U} G(x-y) \leq G(o) + G(u) + G(v) + G(w) \leq G(o) + G(e_k) + G(e_l) + G(e_m). \end{equation*} This bound is at most $4 G(o) - 3$ because $G(e_i) = G(o) - 1$ for every $1 \leq i \leq d$ (see, e.g., \cite[Exercise 3.2]{popov2021}). By \eqref{esv bd1a}, $\mathbb{E}_x [N]$ is at most $4 G(o) - 4$. To bound below $\mathbb{E}_x [N \mid N>0]$, we use the fact that $\mathbb{E}_z [N] \geq G(o) - 1$ for every $z \in U$, since $N$ is at least the number of times that random walk returns to $z$. Consequently, \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}_x [N \mid N > 0] & = 1 + \mathbb{E}_x \big[ \mathbb{E}_{S_{\tau_{U}}} [N] \bigm\vert \tau_{U} < \infty \big] \geq G(o). \end{align*} We substitute the preceding bounds into \eqref{esv bd1} to find that \[ \mathrm{esc}_U (x) \geq 1 - \frac{4 G(o) - 4}{G(o)} = \frac{4 - 3G(o)}{G(o)}. \] To bound below the harmonic measure of $x$ in $U$, we note that $\mathrm{cap}_U$ is at most $4G(o)^{-1}$ because $|U| \leq 4$ and because $\mathrm{esc}_U (y)$ is at most $G(o)^{-1}$ for $y \in U$. We combine this fact with the preceding display to find that \[ \mathbb{H}_U (x) = \frac{\mathrm{esc}_U (x)}{\mathrm{cap}_U} \geq \frac{4 - 3G(o)}{4}. \] Since the preceding lower bounds decrease with $G(o)$ and since $G(o) \leq \frac54$ for $d \geq 4$ (Lemma~\ref{g5}), we conclude that $\mathrm{esc}_U (x) \geq \frac15$ and $\mathbb{H}_U (x) \geq \frac{1}{16}$.
nodes.statement_short: Write esc as 1 - E[N]/E[N|N>0] for the number N of returns and bound both using Green's function monotonicity.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Express esc via the number N of returns
nodes.statement_short: Express esc via the number N of returns
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Equation (5.6)
nodes.statement: \mathrm{esc}_U (x) = \mathbb{P}_x (N=0) = 1 - \frac{\mathbb{E}_x [N]}{\mathbb{E}_x [N \mid N > 0]}.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: esv bd1

nodes.name: Bound E[N] by 4G(o)-4 using Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement:
To bound above $\mathbb{E}_x [N]$, we note that
\begin{equation} \mathbb{E}_x [N] = \sum_{y \in U} G(x-y) - 1.
\end{equation}
Since $x \in U$ and $|U| \leq 4$, there are $u, v, w\in \mathbb{Z}^d$ such that
\[
\{x - y: y \in U\} \subseteq \{o, u, v, w\} \quad \text{and} \quad \exists k,l, m \in \{1,\dots,d\}: u \succeq e_k, \,\, v \succeq e_l, \,\, w \succeq e_m.
\]
Green's function is nonnegative and nonincreasing in $\succeq$ (Lemma \ref{gpart}), hence
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{y \in U} G(x-y) \leq G(o) + G(u) + G(v) + G(w) \leq G(o) + G(e_k) + G(e_l) + G(e_m).
\end{equation*}
This bound is at most $4 G(o) - 3$ because $G(e_i) = G(o) - 1$ for every $1 \leq i \leq d$ (see, e.g., \cite[Exercise 3.2]{popov2021}). By \eqref{esv bd1a}, $\mathbb{E}_x [N]$ is at most $4 G(o) - 4$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound E[N] by 4G(o)-4 using Lemma 5.2
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Equation (5.7)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}_x [N] = \sum_{y \in U} G(x-y) - 1.
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: esv bd1a

nodes.name: Bound E[N | N>0] below by G(o)
nodes.statement_short: Bound E[N | N>0] below by G(o)
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Escape probability lower bound
nodes.statement:
We substitute the preceding bounds into \eqref{esv bd1} to find that
\[
\mathrm{esc}_U (x) \geq 1 - \frac{4 G(o) - 4}{G(o)} = \frac{4 - 3G(o)}{G(o)}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Escape probability lower bound
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Divide by the capacity
nodes.statement:
To bound below the harmonic measure of $x$ in $U$, we note that $\mathrm{cap}_U$ is at most $4G(o)^{-1}$ because $|U| \leq 4$ and because $\mathrm{esc}_U (y)$ is at most $G(o)^{-1}$ for $y \in U$. We combine this fact with the preceding display to find that
\[
\mathbb{H}_U (x) = \frac{\mathrm{esc}_U (x)}{\mathrm{cap}_U} \geq \frac{4 - 3G(o)}{4}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Divide by the capacity
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Use G(o) <= 5/4 (Lemma 5.4)
nodes.statement: Since the preceding lower bounds decrease with $G(o)$ and since $G(o) \leq \frac54$ for $d \geq 4$ (Lemma~\ref{g5}), we conclude that $\mathrm{esc}_U (x) \geq \frac15$ and $\mathbb{H}_U (x) \geq \frac{1}{16}$.
nodes.statement_short: Use G(o) <= 5/4 (Lemma 5.4)
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Escape probability lower bound for a small, well-separated part
nodes.statement: Let $d \geq 4$. There is a constant $c = c(d)$ such that, if $U \in \mathrm{Conf}_d$ can be partitioned into $\mathcal{P} = (\mathcal{P}^1, \mathcal{P}^2)$ such that $|\mathcal{P}^1| \leq 4$ and $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P}) \geq \kappa$, then \begin{equation*} \mathrm{esc}_U (x) \geq \left( 1 - c |U| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})^{2-d} \right) \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{P}^1} (x), \quad x \in \mathcal{P}^1. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT
assumptions: $U \in \mathrm{Conf}_d$ can be partitioned into $\mathcal{P} = (\mathcal{P}^1, \mathcal{P}^2)$ such that $|\mathcal{P}^1| \leq 4$ and $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P}) \geq \kappa$
nodes.label: min hm

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $U$ and $\mathcal{P}$ satisfy the hypotheses and let $x \in \mathcal{P}^1$. nodes.name: Proof sketch of Lemma 5.8
nodes.statement:
For the event in \eqref{help est1} to occur, random walk must go from $\mathcal{P}^1$ to $\mathcal{P}^2$ and then from $\mathcal{P}^2$ to $\mathcal{P}^1$. By Lemma~\ref{simple set hit}, it does so with probabilities of roughly $O\left(|\mathcal{P}^1| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})^{2-d} \right)$ and then $O\left( |\mathcal{P}^2| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})^{2-d} \right)$. To prove \eqref{help est2}, we consider the event that random walk from $x$ first escapes $B = A \cup \{y\}$ to a distance of roughly $\mathrm{diam} (B)$ away, before returning to $B$ at $y$. The virtue of this event is that the conditional hitting distribution of $B$ from a distance of roughly $\mathrm{diam} (B)$ away is comparable to the harmonic measure of $B$, which is bounded below by a constant due to Lemma~\ref{min es}. The lower bound \eqref{help est2} is due to the fact that random walk from a distance of $\mathrm{diam} (B)$ from $B$ returns to $B$ with a probability of $\Omega (\mathrm{diam} (B)^{2-d})$ by Lemma~\ref{simple set hit}.

The assumptions on $\mathcal{P}$ ensure that Lemma~\ref{simple set hit} and Lemma~\ref{min es} are applicable. In particular, we assume that $|\mathcal{P}^1| \leq 3$ instead of $|\mathcal{P}^1| \leq 4$ so that $B \cup \{x\} = \mathcal{P}^1 \cup \{y\}$ has at most four elements. This enables our use of Lemma~\ref{min es} to bound below $\mathrm{esc}_{B \cup \{x\}} (x)$ by a constant, which further bounds below the probability that random walk escapes to a distance of roughly $\mathrm{diam} (B)$ away from $B$.
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: (5.8) needs two long crossings, each O(sep^{2-d}); (5.9) forces an excursion to distance ~diam(B) after which landing at y is comparable to harmonic measure.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $U$ and $\mathcal{P}$ satisfy the hypotheses, and let $x \in \mathcal{P}^1$ and $y \in \partial A$. We bound the probability in \eqref{help est1} as \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}_{x} (S_{\tau_A - 1} = y, \tau_{\mathcal{P}^2} < \tau_A < \infty) &\leq \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\mathcal{P}^2} < \tau_A < \infty)\\ &\leq \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\mathcal{P}^2} < \infty) \max_{z \in \mathcal{P}^2} \mathbb{P}_z ( \tau_A < \infty) \lesssim |U| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})^{4-2d}. \end{align*} The first inequality follows from dropping the sub-event $\{S_{\tau_A-1} = y\}$; the second holds because $\max_{z \in \mathcal{P}^2} \mathbb{P}_z (\tau_A < \infty)$ bounds above the conditional hitting probability of $A$ from an arbitrarily distributed $Z$ in $\mathcal{P}^2$; the third follows from two applications of Lemma~\ref{simple set hit}, which applies because $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P}) \geq \kappa$, and the fact that $|\mathcal{P}^1| |\mathcal{P}^2| \leq 3 |U|$. We bound below the probability in \eqref{help est2} using the fact (see, e.g., \cite[Exercise 3.25]{popov2021}) that there is a constant $\lambda > 1$ such that, if the distance between $u \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and a finite set $B \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ is at least $\lambda \mathrm{diam} (B)$, then \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_u (S_{\tau_B} = v \mid \tau_B < \infty) \geq \frac12 \mathbb{H}_B (v), \quad v \in B. \end{equation} To this end, let $B = A \cup \{y\}$ and $C = \{u \in \mathbb{Z}^d: \mathrm{dist} (u, B) \leq \lambda \mathrm{diam} (B)\}$, and note that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A - 1} = y, \tau_A < \infty) \geq \frac{1}{2d} \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B < \infty, S_{\tau_B} = y). \end{equation} In words, the probability that the random walk steps from $y$ when it first returns to $A$ is at least the probability that it does so after hitting $\partial C$. Note that the factor of $\frac{1}{2d}$ addresses the step that the random walk takes from $y$ into $A$ to ensure that $\tau_B = \tau_A - 1$. The lower bound \eqref{hm like bd} factors into \[ \frac{1}{2d} \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B) \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_B < \infty \mid \tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B) \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_B} = y \mid \tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B < \infty). \] We address these factors in turn. First, the probability that random walk hits $\partial C$ before returning to $B$ is at least the probability of escape from $B \cup \{x\}$, which, by Lemma~\ref{min es}, is at least $\frac{1}{5}$ because $|B \cup \{x\}| \leq |\mathcal{P}^1| + 1 \leq 4$: \[ \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B ) \geq \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_B = \infty) \geq \mathrm{esc}_{B \cup \{x\}} (x) \geq \frac15. \] Note that we use $\mathrm{esc}_{B \cup \{x\}} (x)$ instead of $\mathrm{esc}_B (x)$ because if $x \neq y$, then $x \notin B$, hence $\mathrm{esc}_B (x) = 0$ by definition and the bound of Lemma~\ref{min es} does not apply. Second, given that the random walk hits $\partial C$ before $B$, the conditional probability that it subsequently hits $B$ satisfies \[ \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_B < \infty \mid \tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B) \geq \min_{z \in \partial C} \mathbb{P}_z (\tau_B < \infty) \gtrsim \mathrm{diam} (B)^{2-d}. \] The second inequality holds by Lemma~\ref{simple set hit}, which implies that the hitting probability of $B$ from $z \in \partial C$ is $\Omega (\mathrm{dist}(z, B)^{2-d})$, and by the definition of $C$, which implies that $\mathrm{dist} (z, B) \lesssim \mathrm{diam} (B)$ for every such $z$. Third, given that the random walk hits $\partial C$ and then $B$, the conditional hitting probability of $y$ is at least \[ \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_B} = y \mid \tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B < \infty) \geq \min_{z \in \partial C} \mathbb{P}_z (S_{\tau_B} = y \mid \tau_B < \infty) \geq \frac12 \mathbb{H}_B (y) \geq \frac{1}{32}. \] The second inequality holds by \eqref{ex325}; the third by Lemma~\ref{min es}, which applies because $|B| \leq 3$. We multiply the three preceding bounds to conclude that \[ \frac{1}{2d} \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B < \infty, S_{\tau_B} = y) \gtrsim \mathrm{diam} (B)^{2-d}. \] The bound \eqref{help est2} follows from substituting this into \eqref{hm like bd}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound (5.8) by two applications of Lemma 5.1; bound (5.9) by forcing an excursion to distance ~diam(B) and comparing with harmonic measure. Three factors (escape, return, landing at y) are bounded separately.

\[
\frac{1}{2d} \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B) \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_B < \infty \mid \tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B) \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_B} = y \mid \tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B < \infty).
\]

nodes.name: Escape factor at least 1/5 by Lemma 5.5
nodes.statement:
First, the probability that random walk hits $\partial C$ before returning to $B$ is at least the probability of escape from $B \cup \{x\}$, which, by Lemma~\ref{min es}, is at least $\frac{1}{5}$ because $|B \cup \{x\}| \leq |\mathcal{P}^1| + 1 \leq 4$:
\[
\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B ) \geq \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_B = \infty) \geq \mathrm{esc}_{B \cup \{x\}} (x) \geq \frac15.
\]
Note that we use $\mathrm{esc}_{B \cup \{x\}} (x)$ instead of $\mathrm{esc}_B (x)$ because if $x \neq y$, then $x \notin B$, hence $\mathrm{esc}_B (x) = 0$ by definition and the bound of Lemma~\ref{min es} does not apply.

nodes.name: Return factor at least diam(B)^{2-d} by Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement:
Second, given that the random walk hits $\partial C$ before $B$, the conditional probability that it subsequently hits $B$ satisfies
\[
\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_B < \infty \mid \tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B) \geq \min_{z \in \partial C} \mathbb{P}_z (\tau_B < \infty) \gtrsim \mathrm{diam} (B)^{2-d}.
\]
The second inequality holds by Lemma~\ref{simple set hit}, which implies that the hitting probability of $B$ from $z \in \partial C$ is $\Omega (\mathrm{dist}(z, B)^{2-d})$, and by the definition of $C$, which implies that $\mathrm{dist} (z, B) \lesssim \mathrm{diam} (B)$ for every such $z$.
nodes.statement_short: Return factor at least diam(B)^{2-d} by Lemma 5.1
nodes.section: 5 Inputs to the comparison of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Landing factor at least 1/32
nodes.statement:
Third, given that the random walk hits $\partial C$ and then $B$, the conditional hitting probability of $y$ is at least 
\[
\mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_B} = y \mid \tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B < \infty) \geq \min_{z \in \partial C} \mathbb{P}_z (S_{\tau_B} = y \mid \tau_B < \infty) \geq \frac12 \mathbb{H}_B (y) \geq \frac{1}{32}.
\]
The second inequality holds by \eqref{ex325}; the third by Lemma~\ref{min es}, which applies because $|B| \leq 3$.
nodes.statement_short: Landing factor at least 1/32

We multiply the three preceding bounds to conclude that
\[
\frac{1}{2d} \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\partial C} < \tau_B < \infty, S_{\tau_B} = y) \gtrsim \mathrm{diam} (B)^{2-d}.
\]
The bound \eqref{help est2} follows from substituting this into \eqref{hm like bd}.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $U$ and $\mathcal{P}$ satisfy the hypotheses, and let $x \in U$ and $i = [x]_\mathcal{P}$. Define the coarser partition $\mathcal{C} = (\mathcal{C}^1, \mathcal{C}^2)$ by $\mathcal{C}^1 = \mathcal{P}^i$ and $\mathcal{C}^2 = \mathcal{P}^{\neq i}$, which satisfies $|\mathcal{C}^1| \leq 3$ and $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}) \geq \kappa$. By Lemma~\ref{min hm} and the fact that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}) \geq \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})$, there is a constant $c = c(d)$ such that \[ \mathrm{esc}_U (x) \geq \big(1 - c |U| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})^{2-d} \big) \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{P}^i} (x) \geq \big(1 - c |U| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})^{2-d} \big) \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{P}^i} (x). \] We divide by $\mathrm{cap}_U$ to bound below $\mathbb{H}_U (x)$: \[ \mathbb{H}_U (x) = \frac{\mathrm{esc}_U (x)}{\mathrm{cap}_U} \geq \big(1 - c |U| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})^{2-d} \big) \frac{\mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{P}^i} (x)}{\mathrm{cap}_U} \geq \big(1 - c |U| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})^{2-d} \big) \mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{P}} (i,x). \] The second inequality uses the bound $\mathrm{cap}_U \leq \mathrm{cap}_\mathcal{P}$, which follows from the fact that $\mathrm{esc}_U (y) \leq \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{P}^j} (y)$ for every $1 \leq j \leq k$ and $y \in \mathcal{P}^j$, and the definition of $\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{P}} (i,x)$.

nodes.name: Divide by capacity
nodes.statement:
We divide by $\mathrm{cap}_U$ to bound below $\mathbb{H}_U (x)$:
\[
\mathbb{H}_U (x) = \frac{\mathrm{esc}_U (x)}{\mathrm{cap}_U} \geq \big(1 - c |U| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})^{2-d} \big) \frac{\mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{P}^i} (x)}{\mathrm{cap}_U} \geq \big(1 - c |U| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})^{2-d} \big) \mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{P}} (i,x).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Divide by capacity
nodes.section: 6 Comparison of activation and transport components

nodes.name: Capacity of U is at most that of the partition
nodes.statement: The second inequality uses the bound $\mathrm{cap}_U \leq \mathrm{cap}_\mathcal{P}$, which follows from the fact that $\mathrm{esc}_U (y) \leq \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{P}^j} (y)$ for every $1 \leq j \leq k$ and $y \in \mathcal{P}^j$, and the definition of $\mathbb{H}_{\mathcal{P}} (i,x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Capacity of U is at most that of the partition
nodes.section: 6 Comparison of activation and transport components

nodes.name: Transport comparison
nodes.statement: Let $a \geq \kappa$, $b > 0$, and $d \geq 4$. There is a constant $c = c(b,d)$ such that, if $U \in \mathrm{Conf}_d$ has an $(a,b)$ DOT clustering $\mathcal{P}$, then, for every $x \in U$ and every $y$ in the exterior boundary of $A = \mathcal{P}^{[x]_{\mathcal{P}}} {\setminus} \{x\}$, \begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_{U {\setminus} \{x\}}-1} = y \,\vert\, \tau_{U {\setminus} \{x\}} < \infty) \geq \left(1 - c |U| \left( \frac{\log \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})}{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P})} \right)^{d-2} \right) \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A-1} = y \,\vert\, \tau_A < \infty). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: HAT's transport probability to the boundary of the activated cluster dominates the intracluster transport probability up to 1-O(|U|(log sep/sep)^{d-2}).
nodes.section: 6 Comparison of activation and transport components
nodes.label: prop t comp

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $U$ and $\mathcal{P}$ satisfy the hypotheses, let $x \in U$ and $y \in \partial A$, and let $i = [x]_{\mathcal{P}}$. Define the coarser partition $\mathcal{C} = (\mathcal{C}^1, \mathcal{C}^2)$ by $\mathcal{C}^1 = \mathcal{P}^i$ and $\mathcal{C}^2 = \mathcal{P}^{\neq i}$, which satisfies $A \subset \mathcal{C}^1$, $|\mathcal{C}^1| \leq 3$, and $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}) \geq \kappa$. For brevity, denote $\tau = \tau_{U \setminus\{x\}}$. Following \eqref{ict hat}, the probability in question can be expressed as \begin{multline} \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau-1} = y \,|\, \tau < \infty) = \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A-1} = y \,|\, \tau_A < \infty)\\ \times \underbrace{\frac{\mathbb{P}_{x} (\tau_A < \infty)}{\mathbb{P}_{x} (\tau < \infty)}}_{( \ref{inc hat1} \text{a})} \Bigg( 1 - \underbrace{\frac{\mathbb{P}_{x} (S_{\tau_A-1} = y, \tau_{\mathcal{C}^2} < \tau_A < \infty)}{\mathbb{P}_{x} (S_{\tau_A-1} =y, \tau_A < \infty)}}_{( \ref{inc hat1} \text{b})} \Bigg). \end{multline} To bound below (\ref{inc hat1}a), note that $\tau = \min \{\tau_A, \tau_{\mathcal{C}^2}\}$, so lower and upper bounds of $\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A < \infty) \geq p_1$ and $\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\mathcal{C}^2} < \infty) \leq p_2$ for some $p_1, p_2 \in (0,1]$ would imply that \begin{equation} \frac{\mathbb{P}_{x} (\tau_A < \infty)}{\mathbb{P}_{x} (\tau < \infty)} \geq \frac{\mathbb{P}_{x} (\tau_A < \infty)}{\mathbb{P}_{x} (\tau_A < \infty) + \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{\mathcal{C}^2} < \infty)} \geq 1 - \frac{p_2}{p_1}. \end{equation} By Lemma~\ref{simple set hit}, the fact that $\mathrm{dist} (x,A) \leq \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{C}^1)$, and the assumption that $\mathcal{P}$ is a $(\cdot,b)$ clustering, \[ \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A < \infty) \gtrsim \mathrm{dist}(x, A)^{2-d} \gtrsim \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{C}^1)^{2-d} \gtrsim \left( b \log \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}) \right)^{2-d}. \] By \eqref{eq simple set hit ub} of Lemma~\ref{simple set hit}, which applies because $\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{C}^2) \geq \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}) \geq \kappa$, and the fact that $|\mathcal{C}^2| \leq |U|$, \[ \mathbb{P}_{x} (\tau_{\mathcal{C}^2} < \infty) \lesssim |U| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})^{2-d}. \] We take $p_1$ and $p_2$ to be the preceding lower and upper bounds (including the implicit constants). Substituting these choices into \eqref{618a bd} yields \begin{equation*} \frac{\mathbb{P}_{x} (\tau_A < \infty)}{\mathbb{P}_{x} (\tau < \infty)} \geq 1 - c_1 b^{d-2} |U| \left( \frac{\log \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})}{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})} \right)^{d-2}, \end{equation*} for a constant $c_1 = c_1 (d)$. To bound above (\ref{inc hat1}b), we use Lemma~\ref{lemma help est} with $\mathcal{C}$ in the place of $\mathcal{P}$. The lemma is applicable because $|\mathcal{C}^1| \leq 3$ and $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}) \geq \kappa$. It implies that \[ \frac{\mathbb{P}_{x} (S_{\tau_A-1} = y, \tau_{\mathcal{C}^2} < \tau_A < \infty)}{\mathbb{P}_{x} (S_{\tau_A-1} =y, \tau_A < \infty)} \lesssim |U| \left( \frac{\mathrm{diam}(A \cup \{y\})}{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})^2} \right)^{d-2} \leq c_2 b^{d-2} |U| \left( \frac{\log \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})}{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})^2} \right)^{d-2}, \] for a constant $c_2 = c_2 (d)$. The second inequality holds because the diameter of $A \cup \{y\}$ is at most $\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{C}^1) + 1$, since $y \in \partial A$ and $A \subset \mathcal{C}^1$, and because the diameter of $\mathcal{C}^1 = \mathcal{P}^i$ is at most $b \log \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})$, since $\mathcal{P}$ is a $(\cdot,b)$ clustering. We substitute the bounds on (\ref{inc hat1}a) and (\ref{inc hat1}b) into \eqref{inc hat1} to conclude that \[ \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau-1} = y \,\vert\, \tau < \infty) \geq \left(1 - c b^{d-2} |U| \left( \frac{\log \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})}{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})} \right)^{d-2} \right) \mathbb{P}_x (S_{\tau_A-1} = y \,\vert\, \tau_A < \infty), \] where $c = 2 \max\{c_1,c_2\} b^{d-2}$. This implies the claimed bound because $\frac{\log r}{r}$ decreases with $r > e$ and $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})$ is at least $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{P}) \geq \kappa > e$.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the transport probability as in (4.5) and bound the two correction factors with Lemmas 5.1 and 5.8.

nodes.name: Lower bound on hitting A

By Lemma~\ref{simple set hit}, the fact that $\mathrm{dist} (x,A) \leq \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{C}^1)$, and the assumption that $\mathcal{P}$ is a $(\cdot,b)$ clustering, 
\[
\mathbb{P}_x (\tau_A < \infty) \gtrsim \mathrm{dist}(x, A)^{2-d} \gtrsim \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{C}^1)^{2-d} \gtrsim \left( b \log \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}) \right)^{2-d}.
\]

\[
\mathbb{P}_{x} (\tau_{\mathcal{C}^2} < \infty) \lesssim |U| \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})^{2-d}.
\]

To bound above (\ref{inc hat1}b), we use Lemma~\ref{lemma help est} with $\mathcal{C}$ in the place of $\mathcal{P}$. The lemma is applicable because $|\mathcal{C}^1| \leq 3$ and $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}) \geq \kappa$. It implies that
\[
\frac{\mathbb{P}_{x} (S_{\tau_A-1} = y, \tau_{\mathcal{C}^2} < \tau_A < \infty)}{\mathbb{P}_{x} (S_{\tau_A-1} =y, \tau_A < \infty)} \lesssim |U| \left( \frac{\mathrm{diam}(A \cup \{y\})}{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})^2} \right)^{d-2} \leq c_2 b^{d-2} |U| \left( \frac{\log \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})}{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})^2} \right)^{d-2},
