nodes.name: All (a,b) DOT clusterings of n-element configurations
nodes.statement: We denote the collection of $(a,b)$ DOT clusterings of $n$-element configurations in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by $\mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet = \cup_{U \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}} \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet (U)$.

nodes.name: Growing sequences of DOT clusterings
Equation (7.1)
nodes.statement: \mathrm{Grow}_{a,b,\delta} = \left\{ (\mathcal{C}_t)_{t \geq 0} \in (\mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet)^{\mathbb{N}}: \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_t) \geq t^{\frac12-\delta} \,\,\text{for every $t \geq 0$} \right\}.
nodes.label: event grow

nodes.name: HAT law from a clustering
nodes.statement: Given a clustering $\mathcal{C} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet$, we will use $\mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}}$ to denote the distribution of HAT from the configuration $\cup_i \mathcal{C}^i$.

nodes.name: Natural partitioning under P_C
nodes.statement: Under $\mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}}$, we will use $(\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ to denote the natural partitioning of $(U_t)_{t \geq 0}$ with $\mathcal{C}$.

nodes.name: Main approximation result
nodes.statement: Fix $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$. Let $b > 0$ and let $\delta \in (0, \frac12 - \frac{1}{d-2})$. For every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, there is a constant $\alpha = \alpha (b,d,n,\delta,\epsilon) > 1$ such that, if $a \geq \alpha$, then, for every $\mathcal{C} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet$, \[ \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}} \left( (\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{a,b,\delta} \right) \geq (1 - \varepsilon) \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}} \left( (\mathcal{V}_t)_{t \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{a,b,\delta} \right). \]
nodes.statement_short: Probability that HAT's natural partitioning separates at rate $t^{1/2-\delta}$ is at least $(1-\varepsilon)$ times the IHAT probability.
nodes.label: pe to qe

nodes.name: One-step approximation
nodes.statement: Fix $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$, and let $a,b > 0$. There are constants $\alpha_0 = \alpha_0 (b,d,n)$ and $c = c(b,d,n)$ such that, if $a \geq \alpha_0$, then, for every $\mathcal{C}_0, \mathcal{C}_1 \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet$, \begin{equation} \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} (\mathcal{U}_1 = \mathcal{C}_1) \geq \left( 1 - c \left(a^{-1} \log a\right)^{d-2} \right) \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} (\mathcal{V}_1 = \mathcal{C}_1). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: One HAT step between two separated DOT clusterings is at least $1-c(a^{-1}\log a)^{d-2}$ times the IHAT probability.
nodes.label: p to q

nodes.name: Equation (7.2)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} (\mathcal{U}_1 = \mathcal{C}_1) \geq \left( 1 - c \left(a^{-1} \log a\right)^{d-2} \right) \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} (\mathcal{V}_1 = \mathcal{C}_1).
nodes.label: eq p to q

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha_0$ and $c$ be the constants from Proposition~\ref{p to q} and assume that $a \geq \alpha_0$. For $t \geq 0$, denote \[ g(t) = \max\left\{a, t^{\frac12 - \delta}\right\} \quad \text{and} \quad h (t) = \prod_{s=0}^{t-1} \left(1 - c \left( g(s)^{-1} \log g(s) \right)^{d-2} \right). \] If $(\mathcal{D}_s)_{s \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{a,b,\delta}$, then $g(t)$ is a lower bound on the separation of $\mathcal{D}_t$, so the Markov property and the one-step approximation (Proposition~\ref{p to q}) imply that $h(t)$ satisfies \begin{equation} \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{U}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, s \leq t \right) \geq h(t) \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{V}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, s \leq t \right). \end{equation} If $\delta < \frac12 - \frac{1}{d-2}$, then $h(t) \geq 1 - o_a (1)$. Indeed, some simple but tedious algebra shows that, due to the condition on $\delta$, there are constants $\eta = \eta (d,\delta) > 0$ and $\alpha_1 = \alpha_1 (d, \eta)$ such that, if $a \geq \alpha_1$, then \[ c\sum_{s = 0}^\infty \left( \frac{\log g(s)}{g(s)} \right)^{d-2} \leq O \left(a^{-\eta}\right). \] Here, the implicit constant depends on all parameters: $b$, $d$, $n$, and $\delta$. This bound implies that $h(t)$ decreases to a limit of $h_\infty = 1 - O (a^{-\eta})$ as $t \to \infty$. We apply \eqref{multistep h} to conclude that \begin{align*} \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( (\mathcal{U}_s)_{s \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{a,b,\delta} \right) &= \sum \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{U}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, s \geq 0 \right)\\ &= \sum \lim_{t \to \infty} \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{U}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, 0 \leq s \leq t\right)\\ &\geq h_\infty \sum \lim_{t \to \infty} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{V}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, 0 \leq s \leq t\right)\\ &= h_\infty \sum \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{V}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, s \geq 0\right)\\ &= h_\infty \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( (\mathcal{V}_s)_{s \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{a,b,\delta} \right), \end{align*} where the sums range over $(\mathcal{D}_s)_{s \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{a,b,\delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate the one-step approximation along sequences in Grow and show the product of error factors stays near 1.

nodes.name: Define the separation floor g and error product h
nodes.statement:
Let $\alpha_0$ and $c$ be the constants from Proposition~\ref{p to q} and assume that $a \geq \alpha_0$. For $t \geq 0$, denote 
\[
g(t) = \max\left\{a, t^{\frac12 - \delta}\right\} \quad \text{and} \quad h (t) = \prod_{s=0}^{t-1} \left(1 - c \left( g(s)^{-1} \log g(s) \right)^{d-2} \right).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Define the separation floor g and error product h

nodes.name: Multi-step comparison via Proposition 7.2 and the Markov property
nodes.statement_short: Multi-step comparison via Proposition 7.2 and the Markov property

nodes.name: Equation (7.3)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{U}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, s \leq t \right) \geq h(t) \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{V}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, s \leq t \right).
nodes.label: multistep h

nodes.name: The error product converges to 1-O(a^{-eta})
nodes.statement:
If $\delta < \frac12 - \frac{1}{d-2}$, then $h(t) \geq 1 - o_a (1)$. Indeed, some simple but tedious algebra shows that, due to the condition on $\delta$, there are constants $\eta = \eta (d,\delta) > 0$ and $\alpha_1 = \alpha_1 (d, \eta)$ such that, if $a \geq \alpha_1$, then
\[
c\sum_{s = 0}^\infty \left( \frac{\log g(s)}{g(s)} \right)^{d-2} \leq O \left(a^{-\eta}\right).
\]
Here, the implicit constant depends on all parameters: $b$, $d$, $n$, and $\delta$. This bound implies that $h(t)$ decreases to a limit of $h_\infty = 1 - O (a^{-\eta})$ as $t \to \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: The error product converges to 1-O(a^{-eta})

nodes.name: Sum over sequences in Grow
nodes.statement:
We apply \eqref{multistep h} to conclude that
\begin{align*}
\mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( (\mathcal{U}_s)_{s \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{a,b,\delta} \right)
&= \sum \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{U}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, s \geq 0 \right)\\ 
&= \sum \lim_{t \to \infty} \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{U}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, 0 \leq s \leq t\right)\\ 
&\geq h_\infty \sum \lim_{t \to \infty} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{V}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, 0 \leq s \leq t\right)\\ 
&= h_\infty \sum \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathcal{V}_s = \mathcal{D}_s, s \geq 0\right)\\ 
&= h_\infty \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( (\mathcal{V}_s)_{s \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{a,b,\delta} \right), 
\end{align*}
where the sums range over $(\mathcal{D}_s)_{s \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{a,b,\delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over sequences in Grow

nodes.name: The *-adjacency graph
nodes.statement: To state it, denote by $\mathbb{Z}^{d\ast}$ the graph with vertex set $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and with an edge between distinct $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ when $x$ and $y$ differ by at most one in each coordinate.
nodes.section: 7.1 An equivalence between the possible transitions of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: *-visible boundary
nodes.section: 7.1 An equivalence between the possible transitions of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Equation (7.4)
nodes.statement: \partial_{\mathrm{vis}} A = \big\{x \in \mathbb{Z}^d: \text{$x$ is adjacent in $\mathbb{Z}^{d\ast}$ to some $y \in A$}\\ \text{and there is a path from $\infty$ to $x$ disjoint from $A$} \big\}.
nodes.section: 7.1 An equivalence between the possible transitions of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: bdyvis

nodes.name: Kesten's lemma on the *-visible boundary
nodes.statement: If $A$ is a finite, $\ast$-connected subset of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, then $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} A$ is connected in $\mathbb{Z}^d$.
nodes.section: 7.1 An equivalence between the possible transitions of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: kesten result

nodes.name: Exposed element (via escape probability)
nodes.statement: For a finite set $A \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ and $x \in A$, we say that $x$ is exposed in $A$ if $\mathrm{esc}_A (x) > 0$.
nodes.section: 7.1 An equivalence between the possible transitions of HAT and IHAT

nodes.name: Exposure in a cluster implies exposure in the union
nodes.statement: Fix $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$. Let $a, b > 0$, and let $\mathcal{C} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet$. If $a \geq \max\{e^{2b},8\sqrt{d}\}$, then \begin{align*} \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{C}^i} (x) > 0 \implies \mathrm{esc}_{\cup_j \mathcal{C}^j} (x) > 0, \quad x \in \mathbb{Z}^d. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 7.1 An equivalence between the possible transitions of HAT and IHAT
nodes.label: help for at pairs

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $x$ be exposed in $\mathcal{C}^i$ and denote the union of clusters by $U = \cup_j \mathcal{C}^j$. To prove that $x$ is exposed in $U$, it suffices to show that there is a path from $x$ to the boundary of \[ F = \{ z \in \mathbb{Z}^d: \mathrm{dist} (z, U ) \leq 2 \mathrm{diam} ( U ) \}, \] which otherwise lies outside of $U$. Because $x$ is exposed in $\mathcal{C}^i$, there is a path $\Gamma$ from $x$ to $\partial F$, which otherwise lies outside of $\mathcal{C}^i$. We modify $\Gamma$ to obtain a path that otherwise lies outside of the rest of $U$ as well. To this end, let \[ F_j = \big\{ z \in \mathbb{Z}^d: \mathrm{dist} (z,\mathcal{C}^j) \leq \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{C}^j) \big\}, \quad 1 \leq j \leq \# \mathcal{C}. \] We make use of two facts about the $F_j$. {\bf Fact 1}.\ Each $F_j$ is finite and $\ast$-connected, so each $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} F_j$ is connected by Lemma \ref{kesten result}. {\bf Fact 2}.\ If $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})$ is at least $\max\{e^{2b},8\sqrt{d}\}$, then each $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} F_j$ is disjoint from $\cup_k F_k$. To see why, note that any element of $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} F_j$ is within $\sqrt{d}$ of an element of $F_j$, while the distance between distinct $F_j$ and $F_k$ exceeds $\sqrt{d}$: \begin{align*} \mathrm{dist} (F_j,F_k) & \geq \mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{C}^j,\mathcal{C}^k) - \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{C}^j) - \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{C}^k) - 2\sqrt{d}\\ & \geq \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{C}^j,\mathcal{C}^k) \Big( 1 - \frac{2b \log \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{C}^j,\mathcal{C}^k) + 2\sqrt{d}}{\mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{C}^j,\mathcal{C}^k)} \Big) > \sqrt{d}. \end{align*} The first inequality follows from the triangle inequality; the second from the fact that $\mathcal{C}$ is a $(\cdot,b)$ clustering; the third from the fact that the ratio is decreasing in $\mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{C}^j, \mathcal{C}^k)$, which is at least $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C})$, and some simple algebra using the assumption that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}) \geq \max\{e^{2b},8\sqrt{d}\}$. Assume that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}) \geq \max\{e^{2b},8\sqrt{d}\}$. We will keep the part of $\Gamma$ from $x$ until it first encounters $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} F_i$, which otherwise avoids $\cup_k F_k$ by assumption. We denote by $J$ the set of labels of the $F_j$ subsequently hit by $\Gamma$. If $J$ is empty, then we are done. Otherwise, let $\ell$ be the label of the first of the $F_j$ that $\Gamma$ hits, and let $\Gamma_u$ and $\Gamma_v$ be the first and last elements of $\Gamma$ which intersect $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} F_\ell$. By Fact 1, $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} F_\ell$ is connected, so there is a shortest path $\Lambda$ in $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} F_\ell$ from $\Gamma_u$ to $\Gamma_v$. We then edit $\Gamma$ to form $\Gamma'$ as \[ \Gamma' = \big( \Gamma_1, \dots, \Gamma_{u-1}, \Lambda_1, \dots, \Lambda_{|\Lambda|}, \Gamma_{v+1}, \dots, \Gamma_{|\Gamma|} \big).\] Because $\Gamma_{v+1}$ was the last element of $\Gamma$ which intersected $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} F_\ell$, $\Gamma'$ avoids $F_\ell$. By Fact 2, $\Lambda$ avoids $\cup_k F_k$, so if $J'$ is the set of labels of $F_j$ encountered by $\Gamma'$, then $|J'| \leq |J|-1$. If $J'$ is empty, then we are done. Otherwise, we can relabel $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$ and $J$ to $J'$ in the preceding argument to continue inductively, obtaining $\Gamma''$ and $|J''| \leq |J|-2$, and so on. Because $|J| \leq |U|$, we need to modify the path at most $|U|$ times before the resulting path to $\partial F$ does not return to $\cup_k F_k$ after reaching $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} F_i$. In summary, we edited $\Gamma$ to obtain a path from $x$ to $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} F_i$ and then from $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} F_i$ to $\partial F$, which otherwise avoids $U$. We conclude that $x$ is exposed in $U$.

nodes.name: Equivalence between possible transitions
nodes.statement: Fix $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$. Let $a,b > 0$, let $\mathcal{C}_0, \mathcal{C}_1 \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet$, and denote $U_0 = \cup_j \mathcal{C}_0^j$. nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $a,b$ and $\mathcal{C}_0, \mathcal{C}_1$ satisfy the hypotheses, let $x \in U_0$ and $y \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ satisfy \eqref{c0 to c1 equiv}, and denote $U_1 = \cup_j \mathcal{C}_1^j$ and $i = [x]_{\mathcal{C}_0}$. Observe that \begin{subnumcases}{p_{U_0} (x,y) > 0 \iff} \mathrm{esc}_{U_0} (x) > 0, \\ \mathrm{esc}_{U_1} (y) > 0, \,\,\text{and} \\ y \in \partial \big( U_0 {\setminus} \{x\} \big). \end{subnumcases} Analogously, \begin{subnumcases}{q_{\mathcal{C}_0} (i,x,y) > 0 \iff} \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{C}_0^i} (x) > 0, \\ \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{C}_1^i} (y) > 0, \,\,\text{and} \\ y \in \partial \big( \mathcal{C}_0^i {\setminus} \{x\} \big). \end{subnumcases} We claim that \[ \eqref{p.1} \iff \eqref{q.1}, \,\, \eqref{p.2} \iff \eqref{q.2}, \,\,\text{and}\,\, \eqref{p.3} \iff \eqref{q.3}, \] which together imply \eqref{corresp}. We address the forward implications first. \textbf{Forward implications}. Because $x \in \mathcal{C}_0^i \subseteq U_0$ and $y \in \mathcal{C}_1^i \subseteq U_1$, \[ \mathrm{esc}_{U_0} (x) \leq \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{C}_0^i} (x) \,\,\text{and}\,\, \mathrm{esc}_{U_1} (y) \leq \mathrm{esc}_{\mathcal{C}_1^i} (y), \] hence $\eqref{p.1} \implies \eqref{q.1}$ and $\eqref{p.2} \implies \eqref{q.2}$. Next, because $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) \geq a > 1$, we have \[ \partial \big( U_0 {\setminus} \{x\} \big) = \partial \Big( \bigcup_i \mathcal{C}_0^i {\setminus} \{x\} \Big) = \bigcup_i \partial \big( \mathcal{C}_0^i {\setminus}\{x\} \big). \] Consequently, \eqref{p.3} implies that $y \in \partial \big( \mathcal{C}_0^j {\setminus} \{x\} \big)$ for at least one choice of $j$. In fact, $j = i$ is the only choice that works as, otherwise, we would have $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_1) = 1$. We conclude that $\eqref{p.3} \implies \eqref{q.3}$. \textbf{Reverse implications}. Because $\mathcal{C}_0$ and $\mathcal{C}_1$ are $(a,b)$ separated for an $a$ which is at least $\max\{e^{2b},8\sqrt{d}\}$, Proposition \ref{help for at pairs} applies with $\mathcal{C}_0$ or $\mathcal{C}_1$ in the place of $\mathcal{C}$. Using it, we conclude that $\eqref{p.1} \impliedby \eqref{q.1}$ and $\eqref{p.2} \impliedby \eqref{q.2}$. The argument we used for the last forward implication applies in reverse to show that $\eqref{p.3} \impliedby \eqref{q.3}$.

\textbf{Forward implications}. Because $x \in \mathcal{C}_0^i \subseteq U_0$ and $y \in \mathcal{C}_1^i \subseteq U_1$,

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Recall the constant $\kappa$ that appears in the statements of Propositions~\ref{prop h comp} and \ref{prop t comp}. Let $b > 0$ and $a \geq \max \{e^{2b},8\sqrt{d}, \kappa\}$, let $\mathcal{C}_0, \mathcal{C}_1 \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet$, and denote $U_0 = \cup_j \mathcal{C}_0^j$. By the definition of the natural partitioning of HAT with $\mathcal{C}_0$ (Definition~\ref{nat part}), \begin{equation} \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} (\mathcal{U}_1 = \mathcal{C}_1) = \sum p_{U_0} (x,y), \end{equation} where the sum ranges over $x \in U_0$ and $y \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ that satisfy $\mathcal{C}_1 = (\mathcal{C}_0 \sd{[x]_{\mathcal{C}_0}} \{x\}) \cup^{[x]_{\mathcal{C}_0}} \{y\}$. According to Proposition~\ref{at pairs}, since $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0)$ is at least $\max \{e^{2b}, 8 \sqrt{d}\}$, the summand in \eqref{sum puo} is positive if and only if $q_{\mathcal{C}_0} ([x]_{\mathcal{C}_0},x,y)$ is. Moreover, since $\mathcal{C}_0$ is a partition of $U_0$, $q_{\mathcal{C}_0} (j,x,y) = 0$ for every $j \neq [x]_{\mathcal{C}_0}$. Hence, \begin{equation} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} (\mathcal{V}_1 = \mathcal{C}_1) = \sum q_{\mathcal{C}_0} ([x]_{\mathcal{C}_0},x,y), \end{equation} where the sum ranges over the same $x$ and $y$ as in \eqref{sum puo}. Since $\mathcal{C}_0$ is a DOT clustering with a separation of at least $a \geq \kappa$, Propositions~\ref{prop h comp} and \ref{prop t comp} together imply that there is a constant $c = c (b,d,n)$ such that \begin{equation} p_{U_0} (x,y) \geq \left(1 - c \left( a^{-1} \log a \right)^{d-2} \right) q_{\mathcal{C}_0} ([x]_{\mathcal{C}_0},x,y). \end{equation} We apply this bound to \eqref{sum puo} and then use \eqref{sum quo} to conclude that \[ \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}_0} (\mathcal{U}_1 = \mathcal{C}_1) \geq \left(1 - c \left( a^{-1} \log a \right)^{d-2} \right) \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} (\mathcal{V}_1 = \mathcal{C}_1). \]

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Assume that $\xi_m \leq t < \xi_{m+1}$. By \eqref{tri app both}, \begin{equation} \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_t^i, \mathcal{V}_t^j) \geq \|M_t^i - M_t^j\| - \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_t^i) - \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_t^j). \end{equation} To replace $M_t^i - M_t^j$ by $S_m^{i,j} = M_{\xi_m}^i - M_{\xi_m}^j$ in \eqref{tri app}, we bound the norm of their difference: \begin{equation} M_t^i - M_t^j - (M_{\xi_m}^i - M_{\xi_m}^j) = \sum_{s = \xi_m}^{t-1} \left( M_{s+1}^i - M_{s+1}^j - (M_s^i - M_s^j) \right). \end{equation} Taking the norm of both sides and applying \eqref{sep by one} gives \begin{align*} \| M_t^i - M_t^j - (M_{\xi_m}^i - M_{\xi_m}^j) \| &\leq \sum_{s = \xi_m}^{t-1} \max \{\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i), \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^j)\}\\ &\leq \sum_{s = \xi_m}^{t-1} (2+s-\xi_m) \leq \frac12 (t - \xi_m)^2 \leq \frac12 (\xi_{m+1} - \xi_m)^2. \end{align*} The second inequality holds because cluster diameter grows by at most one with each step and because, at time $\xi_m$, the clusters have diameters of at most $2$, since they belong to $\mathrm{Ref}$. The fourth inequality holds because $t < \xi_{m+1}$. The preceding bound addresses the first term of \eqref{tri app}. To address the other terms, we use \eqref{diam by one}: \[ \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_t^i) + \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_t^j) \leq (\xi_{m+1} - \xi_m) + \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_{\xi_m}^i) + \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_{\xi_m}^j) \leq 5 (\xi_{m+1} - \xi_m). \] The second inequality holds because $\xi_{m+1} - \xi_m \geq 1$ and because, at time $\xi_m$, the clusters have diameters of at most $2$. Substituting the preceding bounds into \eqref{tri app} gives \[ \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_t^i, \mathcal{V}_t^j) \geq \big\| S_m^{i,j} \big\| - \frac12 (\xi_{m+1} - \xi_m)^2 - 5 (\xi_{m+1} - \xi_m). \] The claimed bound \eqref{eq amlg2} follows from $\xi_{m+1} - \xi_m \geq 1$.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{hm small parts} states that we can activate any element of any cluster of $\mathcal{V}_t$ with a probability of at least $(16n)^{-1}$, since each cluster has two or three elements under $\mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0}$. To arrange a cluster of $\mathcal{V}_t$ into a reference cluster, we first ensure that it is connected, possibly by activating one or two isolated elements, and then we dictate up to two additional IHAT steps to organize the connected cluster into a line segment parallel to $e_1$. After addressing the first cluster of $\mathcal{V}_t$, we apply the same procedure to the rest of the clusters. Consider an arbitrary cluster $\mathcal{V}_t^i$. The following procedure shows that $\mathcal{V}_{t+4}^i \in \mathrm{Ref}$ with a probability of at least $p^4$, where $p = (16n)^{-1} (2d)^{-4}$. \begin{enumerate} \item If there is an isolated element of $\mathcal{V}_t^i$, activate it (w.p.\ $\geq (16n)^{-1}$). Otherwise, ``keep'' the current cluster by transporting to wherever activation occurs (w.p.\ $\geq (16n\cdot 2d)^{-1}$). Repeat this step to ensure that the resulting cluster is connected. \item Once the cluster $\mathcal{V}_{t+2}^i$ is connected, if it does not belong to $\mathrm{Ref}$, activate any element with the least $e_1$ component and transport it to $x+e_1$, where $x$ is any element of $\mathcal{V}_{t+2}^i$ with the greatest $e_1$ component (w.p.\ $\geq (16n)^{-1} (2d)^{-4}$). Otherwise, keep the current cluster (w.p.\ $\geq (16n \cdot 2d)^{-1})$. Repeat this step to ensure that $\mathcal{V}_{t+4}^i$ belongs to $\mathrm{Ref}$ (i.e., equals $\{x,x+e_1\}$ or $\{x,x+e_1,x+2e_1\}$ for some $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$). \end{enumerate} The factors of $(16n)^{-1}$ arise from the use of Lemma~\ref{hm small parts}; factors of $(2d)^{-1}$ arise from dictating random walk steps during the transport component of the dynamics. We can apply this procedure to the rest of the clusters to ensure that $\mathcal{V}_{t+4\#\mathcal{C}_0} \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$. Note that $\# \mathcal{C}_0$ is at most $\frac{n}{2}$. This implies that \[ \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \big( \xi_1 > t + \tfrac{n}{2} \bigm\vert \xi_1 > t \big) \leq q\] where $q = 1 - p^{n/2}$. Continuing inductively, we find that \[ \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \big( \xi_1 > t \big) \leq q^{[\frac{2t}{n}]} \leq q^{-1} e^{- \gamma_1 t} \] for $\gamma_1 = \tfrac{2}{n} \log \tfrac{1}{q}$. Since $q^{-1} \leq 2$, this implies \eqref{eq xi tail}.
nodes.statement_short: Exhibit a 4-step activation/transport procedure that puts each cluster in reference shape with probability bounded below, then iterate.
nodes.section: 8.3 The reference times of IHAT have exponential tails

nodes.name: Why the standard estimates apply to the associated walks
nodes.statement: These estimates apply because $(S_k^{i,j})_{k \geq 0}$ is a symmetric, aperiodic, and irreducible random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, with increment norms $\|S_{k+1}^{i,j} - S_k^{i,j}\|$ that are exponentially tight. First, it is symmetric because the transition probabilities of IHAT are translation invariant. Second, it is aperiodic because, if $\mathcal{V}_t \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$, then $\mathcal{V}_{t+1} = \mathcal{V}_t$ with positive probability. This is true because, if $\mathcal{V}_t \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$, then every element $x \in \mathcal{V}_t^1$ can be activated with positive probability and has a neighbor, hence it can be transported to its site of activation with positive probability. Third, it is not hard to see that, for any $l \in \{1,\dots,d\}$, $S_1^{i,j} = S_0^{i,j} + e_l$ with positive probability, which implies that this random walk is irreducible on $\mathbb{Z}^d$. Fourth, the norm of the increment $\|S_{k+1}^{i,j} - S_k^{i,j} \|$ is exponentially tight because it is at most $\xi_{k+1}^{i,j} - \xi_k^{i,j}$, which is exponentially tight by Lemma~\ref{xi tail}.
nodes.statement_short: The associated walks are symmetric, aperiodic and irreducible with exponentially tight increments, by translation invariance and Lemma 8.2.
nodes.section: 8.4 Two standard estimates for random walks associated with IHAT

nodes.name: Extension of the cited estimates to exponentially tight increments
nodes.statement: In fact, the results cited from \cite{lawler2010random} assume that the increments of the walk are bounded, and the constants $\gamma_2$ through $\gamma_5$ may in general depend on the increment distribution. However, the proofs of these results apply as written to the case when the norms of the increments are exponentially tight, with the exception that the reference to Proposition 4.3.1 in the proof of Proposition 6.4.2 must be replaced by a reference to Proposition 4.3.5 (all of these are results in \cite{lawler2010random}). Additionally, because there are only three possible increment distributions (corresponding to dimer-dimer, dimer-trimer, and trimer-trimer), we can assume that $\gamma_2$ through $\gamma_5$ are the same for all clusters.
nodes.statement_short: Lawler-Limic's proofs carry over to exponentially tight increments; only three increment laws occur, so constants are uniform.

nodes.name: Doubling schedule t_ell, epsilon_ell, kappa_ell
nodes.statement:
We define $t_0 (a) = 0$, 
\[
t_\ell (a) = [(n\ell \log a)^4 (2^\ell a)^2 ], \quad \epsilon_\ell = (n \ell \log (a))^{-1}, \quad \text{and} \quad \kappa_\ell (a) = \beta \log (n \ell t_\ell (a)), \quad \ell \geq 1,
\]
in terms of a constant $\beta > 0$ that we will later choose in terms of $\gamma_1$ from Lemma~\ref{xi tail}.
nodes.section: 9.1 Definitions of key quantities and events

nodes.name: Doubling time sigma_ell
nodes.statement:
The separation remains above $2^\ell a$ during $\{\sigma_\ell^{i,j}, \dots, t_\ell\}$, where
\[
\sigma_\ell^{i,j} = \inf \{ s \geq t_{\ell-1}: \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j) \geq 2^\ell \epsilon_\ell^{-1} a\}. 
\]
nodes.section: 9.1 Definitions of key quantities and events

nodes.name: Number of returns to Ref by time t
nodes.statement: Consecutive reference times between $\xi_{N(t_{\ell-1})}$ and $\xi_{N(t_\ell)+1}$ never differ by more than $\kappa_\ell$, where $N(t) = |\{m \geq 1: \xi_m \leq t\}|$ denotes the number of returns to $\mathrm{Ref}^\times$ by time $t$.
nodes.section: 9.1 Definitions of key quantities and events

nodes.name: Events G_1, ..., G_4
nodes.statement:
These descriptions correspond to the following events (Figure \ref{fig: eventfig}): 
\begin{align*}
\mathsf{G}_1^{i,j} (\ell) &= \big\{ \sigma^{i,j}_\ell \leq t_\ell \big\},\\ 
\mathsf{G}_2^{i,j} (\ell) &= \big\{ \mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{V}_s^i,\mathcal{V}_s^j) \geq 2^{\ell-1} \epsilon_\ell a  \,\,\,\text{for}\,\,\, t_{\ell-1} \leq s \leq t_\ell \big\},\\
\mathsf{G}_3^{i,j} (\ell) &= \big\{ \mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{V}_s^i,\mathcal{V}_s^j) \geq 2^\ell a \,\,\, \text{for} \,\,\, \sigma^{i,j}_\ell \leq s \leq t_\ell  \big\},\\ 
\mathsf{G}_4 (\ell) &= \big\{ \xi_m - \xi_{m-1} \leq \kappa_\ell \,\,\, \text{for} \,\,\, N (t_{\ell-1}) < m \leq N(t_\ell) + 1\big\}.
\end{align*}
nodes.section: 9.1 Definitions of key quantities and events

nodes.name: Intersections of the G events
nodes.statement:
We denote their intersections as 
\[
\mathsf{G}_k (\ell) = \cap_{i < j} \mathsf{G}_k^{i,j} (\ell), \,\, 1 \leq k \leq 3; \quad \mathsf{G}_k = \cap_{\ell \geq 1} \mathsf{G}_k (\ell), \,\, 1 \leq k \leq 4; \quad \text{and} \quad \mathsf{G} = \cap_{k=1}^4 \mathsf{G}_k.
\]
nodes.section: 9.1 Definitions of key quantities and events

nodes.name: Separation grows when G occurs
nodes.statement: There exists $b = b(d,n) > 0$ such that, for any $\delta \in (0,\frac12)$, there exists $\alpha = \alpha (b,d,n,\delta)$, such that, if $a \geq \alpha$ then, \begin{equation} \mathsf{G} \cap \{\mathcal{V}_0 \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times\} \subseteq \left\{ (\mathcal{V}_t)_{t \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{\tilde a,b,\delta} \right\}, \end{equation} where $\tilde a = a^{0.99}$.
nodes.label: rel sep bd

nodes.name: Equation (9.1)
nodes.statement: \mathsf{G} \cap \{\mathcal{V}_0 \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times\} \subseteq \left\{ (\mathcal{V}_t)_{t \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{\tilde a,b,\delta} \right\},
nodes.label: g v ref

nodes.name: G is typical for IHAT
nodes.statement: There is a constant $\alpha = \alpha (b,d,n)$ such that every $\mathcal{C}_0 \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ with $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) \geq \alpha$ satisfies $\mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} (\mathsf{G}) \geq \frac12$.
nodes.label: tl ntb

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Fix $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$, and let $b > 0$ be the constant from Proposition~\ref{rel sep bd}. It suffices to show that, for any $\delta \in (0,\frac12 - \frac{1}{d-2})$, there is $a > 0$ such that, if $W \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}$ has a clustering $\mathcal{W} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet (W) \cap \mathrm{Ref}^\times$, then the natural clustering $(\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ of $(U_t)_{t \geq 0}$ with $\mathcal{W}$ satisfies \[ \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{W}} \left( (\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{\tilde a, b, \delta} \right) \geq \frac14. \] To this end, fix $\varepsilon = \frac12$ in Proposition~\ref{pe to qe}, and let $\alpha > 1$ be the largest of the constants it names in Propositions~\ref{pe to qe}, \ref{rel sep bd}, and \ref{tl ntb}. Then, take $a = \alpha^{1.1}$, so that $\tilde a = a^{0.99} \geq \alpha$. By Propositions~\ref{pe to qe}, \ref{rel sep bd} and \ref{tl ntb}, we have \[ \mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{W}} \left( (\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{\tilde a, b, \delta} \right) \geq \frac12 \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{W}} \left( (\mathcal{V}_t)_{t \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{\tilde a, b, \delta} \right) \geq \frac12 \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{W}} ( \mathsf{G} ) \geq \frac14. \] Respectively, the hypotheses of these three propositions are satisfied because $\mathcal{W} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{\tilde a,b}^\bullet$ for $\tilde a \geq \alpha$, because $b$ is as in Proposition~\ref{rel sep bd} and $a \geq \alpha$, and because $\mathcal{W} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet \cap \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ for $a \geq \alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Propositions 7.1, 9.1 and 9.2 with epsilon = 1/2.

nodes.name: Reduce to a growth bound for the natural clustering
nodes.statement:
Fix $d \geq 5$ and $n \geq 4$, and let $b > 0$ be the constant from Proposition~\ref{rel sep bd}. It suffices to show that, for any $\delta \in (0,\frac12 - \frac{1}{d-2})$, there is $a > 0$ such that, if $W \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}$ has a clustering $\mathcal{W} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet (W) \cap \mathrm{Ref}^\times$, then the natural clustering $(\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ of $(U_t)_{t \geq 0}$ with $\mathcal{W}$ satisfies
\[
\mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{W}} \left( (\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{\tilde a, b, \delta} \right) \geq \frac14.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a growth bound for the natural clustering

nodes.name: Choose epsilon and a
nodes.statement: To this end, fix $\varepsilon = \frac12$ in Proposition~\ref{pe to qe}, and let $\alpha > 1$ be the largest of the constants it names in Propositions~\ref{pe to qe}, \ref{rel sep bd}, and \ref{tl ntb}. Then, take $a = \alpha^{1.1}$, so that $\tilde a = a^{0.99} \geq \alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose epsilon and a

nodes.name: Chain Propositions 7.1, 9.1, 9.2
nodes.statement:
By Propositions~\ref{pe to qe}, \ref{rel sep bd} and \ref{tl ntb}, we have
\[
\mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{W}} \left( (\mathcal{U}_t)_{t \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{\tilde a, b, \delta} \right) \geq \frac12 \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{W}} \left( (\mathcal{V}_t)_{t \geq 0} \in \mathrm{Grow}_{\tilde a, b, \delta} \right) \geq \frac12 \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{W}} ( \mathsf{G} ) \geq \frac14.
\]
Respectively, the hypotheses of these three propositions are satisfied because $\mathcal{W} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{\tilde a,b}^\bullet$ for $\tilde a \geq \alpha$, because $b$ is as in Proposition~\ref{rel sep bd} and $a \geq \alpha$, and because $\mathcal{W} \in \mathrm{Clust}_{a,b}^\bullet \cap \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ for $a \geq \alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Chain Propositions 7.1, 9.1, 9.2

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We need to show that there is $b > 0$ such that, for any $\delta \in (0,\frac12)$, we can take $a$ sufficiently large to ensure that, when $\mathsf{G}$ occurs, \[ \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s) \geq \tilde a, \quad \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i) \leq b \log \mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j), \quad \text{and} \quad \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s) \geq s^{\frac12 - \delta}, \] for every distinct pair of clusters $1 \leq i < j \leq \# \mathcal{V}_0$ and for every $s \geq 0$. We address these three conditions in turn. \begin{enumerate} \item When $\mathsf{G}_2$ occurs, $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s)$ is at least $\epsilon_1 a$ for every $s \geq 0$. If $a$ is sufficiently large in terms of $n$, then $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}) \geq \tilde a$. \item Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $s \in [t_{\ell-1}, t_\ell]$. Recall that $N (t) = |\{m \geq 1: \xi_m \leq t\}|$ denotes the number of returns to $\mathrm{Ref}^\times$ by time $t$. Since diameter grows at most linearly in time and since $\mathcal{V}_{\xi_{N(s)}}^i \in \mathrm{Ref}$ has a diameter of at most $2$, \begin{equation} \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i) \leq \xi_{N(s)+1} - \xi_{N(s)} + 2. \end{equation} We can obtain a further upper bound on $\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i)$ by noting that, when $\mathsf{G}_4$ occurs, $\xi_{N(s)+1} - \xi_{N(s)}$ is at most $\kappa_\ell$, which is essentially $\log t_\ell$. Recall that $t_\ell \lesssim_n (2^\ell a)^2 \cdot (\ell \log a)^4$. Hence, when $a$ is sufficiently large, \[ \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i) \lesssim_n \ell + \log a. \] On the other hand, when $\mathsf{G}_2$ occurs, $\mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j) \geq 2^{\ell-1} \epsilon_\ell a$, which implies that \[ \log \mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{V}_s^i,\mathcal{V}_s^j) \gtrsim_n \ell + \log a. \] By comparing these bounds, we see that $\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i) \leq b \log \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j)$ holds for all sufficiently large $a$, so long as $b$ is large enough in terms of $n$. \item Let $s \in [t_{\ell-1},t_\ell]$, in which case $s^{1/2 - \delta}$ is at most $t_\ell^{1/2 - \delta} \lesssim (2^\ell a)^{1-2\delta} \cdot (\ell \log a)^{2-4\delta}$. When $\mathsf{G}_2$ occurs, $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s) \gtrsim_n \frac{2^\ell a}{\ell \log a}$, hence $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s)$ is larger by a factor of roughly $(2^\ell a)^{2\delta}$: \[ \frac{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s)}{s^{1/2-\delta}} \geq \frac{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s)}{t_\ell^{1/2-\delta}} \gtrsim_n \frac{(2^\ell a)^{2\delta}}{(\ell \log a)^3}. \] Consequently, we can take $a$ sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$ and $n$ to ensure that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s) \geq s^{\frac12 - \delta}$ (Figure~\ref{fig: sqrtfig}). \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Verify the three clustering conditions on G using G_2 for separation and G_4 for diameter.

nodes.name: Three conditions to verify on G
nodes.statement:
We need to show that there is $b > 0$ such that, for any $\delta \in (0,\frac12)$, we can take $a$ sufficiently large to ensure that, when $\mathsf{G}$ occurs, 
\[
\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s) \geq \tilde a, \quad \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i) \leq b \log \mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j), \quad \text{and} \quad \mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s) \geq s^{\frac12 - \delta},
\]
for every distinct pair of clusters $1 \leq i < j \leq \# \mathcal{V}_0$ and for every $s \geq 0$. We address these three conditions in turn.
nodes.statement_short: Three conditions to verify on G

nodes.name: Absolute separation from G_2
nodes.statement: When $\mathsf{G}_2$ occurs, $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s)$ is at least $\epsilon_1 a$ for every $s \geq 0$. If $a$ is sufficiently large in terms of $n$, then $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}) \geq \tilde a$.
nodes.statement_short: Absolute separation from G_2

nodes.name: Relative diameter bound
nodes.statement:
Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $s \in [t_{\ell-1}, t_\ell]$. Recall that $N (t) = |\{m \geq 1: \xi_m \leq t\}|$ denotes the number of returns to $\mathrm{Ref}^\times$ by time $t$. Since diameter grows at most linearly in time and since $\mathcal{V}_{\xi_{N(s)}}^i \in \mathrm{Ref}$ has a diameter of at most $2$,
\begin{equation} \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i) \leq \xi_{N(s)+1} - \xi_{N(s)} + 2.
\end{equation}
We can obtain a further upper bound on $\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i)$ by noting that, when $\mathsf{G}_4$ occurs, $\xi_{N(s)+1} - \xi_{N(s)}$ is at most $\kappa_\ell$, which is essentially $\log t_\ell$. Recall that $t_\ell \lesssim_n (2^\ell a)^2 \cdot (\ell \log a)^4$. Hence, when $a$ is sufficiently large,
\[
\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i) \lesssim_n \ell + \log a.
\]
On the other hand, when $\mathsf{G}_2$ occurs, $\mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j) \geq 2^{\ell-1} \epsilon_\ell a$, which implies that
\[
\log \mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{V}_s^i,\mathcal{V}_s^j) \gtrsim_n \ell + \log a.
\]
By comparing these bounds, we see that $\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i) \leq b \log \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j)$ holds for all sufficiently large $a$, so long as $b$ is large enough in terms of $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Relative diameter bound

nodes.statement_short: Diameter at most the reference gap plus 2

nodes.name: Equation (9.2)
nodes.statement: \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i) \leq \xi_{N(s)+1} - \xi_{N(s)} + 2.

nodes.name: Gap at most kappa_ell under G_4
nodes.statement:
We can obtain a further upper bound on $\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i)$ by noting that, when $\mathsf{G}_4$ occurs, $\xi_{N(s)+1} - \xi_{N(s)}$ is at most $\kappa_\ell$, which is essentially $\log t_\ell$. Recall that $t_\ell \lesssim_n (2^\ell a)^2 \cdot (\ell \log a)^4$. Hence, when $a$ is sufficiently large,
\[
\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i) \lesssim_n \ell + \log a.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Gap at most kappa_ell under G_4

nodes.name: log distance at least order ell + log a
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, when $\mathsf{G}_2$ occurs, $\mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j) \geq 2^{\ell-1} \epsilon_\ell a$, which implies that
\[
\log \mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{V}_s^i,\mathcal{V}_s^j) \gtrsim_n \ell + \log a.
\]
nodes.statement_short: log distance at least order ell + log a

nodes.name: Choose b large in terms of n
nodes.statement: By comparing these bounds, we see that $\mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_s^i) \leq b \log \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j)$ holds for all sufficiently large $a$, so long as $b$ is large enough in terms of $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose b large in terms of n

nodes.name: Separation beats s^{1/2-delta} for large a
nodes.statement:
Let $s \in [t_{\ell-1},t_\ell]$, in which case $s^{1/2 - \delta}$ is at most $t_\ell^{1/2 - \delta} \lesssim (2^\ell a)^{1-2\delta} \cdot (\ell \log a)^{2-4\delta}$. When $\mathsf{G}_2$ occurs, $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s) \gtrsim_n \frac{2^\ell a}{\ell \log a}$, hence $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s)$ is larger by a factor of roughly $(2^\ell a)^{2\delta}$:
\[
\frac{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s)}{s^{1/2-\delta}} \geq \frac{\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s)}{t_\ell^{1/2-\delta}} \gtrsim_n \frac{(2^\ell a)^{2\delta}}{(\ell \log a)^3}.
\]
Consequently, we can take $a$ sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$ and $n$ to ensure that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{V}_s) \geq s^{\frac12 - \delta}$ (Figure~\ref{fig: sqrtfig}).
nodes.statement_short: Separation beats s^{1/2-delta} for large a

nodes.name: Filtration of IHAT
nodes.statement: To state it, we denote by $\mathscr{F}_t$ the $\sigma$-field generated by $(\mathcal{V}_s)_{0 \leq s \leq t}$.

nodes.name: Expectation under IHAT
nodes.statement: Additionally, throughout this subsection, we use $\mathbf{E}_{\mathcal{C}}$ to denote expectation with respect to $\mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}}$ instead of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathcal{C}}$.

nodes.name: Conditional bound on the failure of G at stage ell
nodes.statement: There exists $\alpha = \alpha (d,n) > 0$ such that, if $\mathcal{C}_0 \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ satisfies $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) \geq \alpha$, then \begin{equation} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{G} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \mid \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) \mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{G}(\ell-1)} \leq 8 \ell^{-2}, \quad \ell \geq 1, \end{equation} where $\eta_{\ell-1}$ denotes $\xi_{N(t_{\ell-1})+1}$.
nodes.label: qg1

nodes.name: Equation (9.3)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{G} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \mid \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) \mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{G}(\ell-1)} \leq 8 \ell^{-2}, \quad \ell \geq 1,
nodes.label: eq qg1

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha > 0$ be the constant named in Proposition~\ref{qg1}, let $\mathcal{C}_0 \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ satisfy $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) \geq \alpha$, and let $\ell \geq 1$. By conditioning on $\mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}}$ and then applying Proposition~\ref{qg1}, we find that \begin{equation*} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \Big( \mathsf{G}(\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \cap_{m=1}^{\ell-1} \mathsf{G} (m) \Big) \leq \mathbf{E}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \, \Big[ \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \big( \mathsf{G} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \mid \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \big) \mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{G} (\ell-1)} \Big] \leq 8\ell^{-2}. \end{equation*} Consequently, \[ \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \Big( \big( \cap_{\ell=1}^\infty \mathsf{G} (\ell) \big)^{\mathsf{c}} \Big) = \sum_{\ell = 1}^\infty \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \Big( \mathsf{G}(\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \cap_{m=1}^{\ell-1} \mathsf{G} (m) \Big) \leq \sum_{\ell=1}^\infty 8 \ell^{-2} < \frac12. \]
nodes.statement_short: Condition on the stage filtration and sum the bounds of Proposition 9.3 over ell.

nodes.name: Condition on the stage filtration and apply Proposition 9.3
nodes.statement_short: Condition on the stage filtration and apply Proposition 9.3

nodes.name: Sum over stages
nodes.statement:
Consequently,
\[
\mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \Big( \big( \cap_{\ell=1}^\infty \mathsf{G} (\ell) \big)^{\mathsf{c}} \Big) = \sum_{\ell = 1}^\infty \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \Big( \mathsf{G}(\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \cap_{m=1}^{\ell-1} \mathsf{G} (m) \Big) \leq \sum_{\ell=1}^\infty 8 \ell^{-2} < \frac12.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Sum over stages

nodes.name: Random-walk analogue rho_ell of sigma_ell
nodes.statement:
This motivates the definition of the following events, in terms of an analogue of $\sigma_\ell^{i,j}$:
\[
\rho_\ell^{i,j} = \inf\big\{m > N (t_{\ell-1}): S_m^{i,j} \notin B \big( 2^{\ell} \epsilon_\ell^{-1} a + 6\kappa_\ell^2 \big)\big\}, \quad \ell \geq 1.
\]

nodes.name: Events F_1, ..., F_4
nodes.statement:
We also use $\kappa_\ell$ to define analogues of $\mathsf{G}_k^{i,j} (\ell)$: 
\begin{align*}
\mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell) &= \big\{ \rho_\ell^{i,j} \leq N (t_\ell) \big\},\\ 
\mathsf{F}_2^{i,j} (\ell) &= \big\{ S_m^{i,j} \notin B \big( 2^{\ell-1} \epsilon_\ell a + 6\kappa_\ell^2 \big),\,\,N (t_{\ell-1}) \leq m \leq N (t_\ell) + 1 \big\},\\  
\mathsf{F}_3^{i,j} (\ell) &= \big\{ S_m^{i,j} \notin B \big( 2^{\ell}a + 6\kappa_\ell^2 \big),\,\, \rho_\ell^{i,j} \leq m \leq N (t_\ell) + 1 \big\},
\end{align*}
and $\mathsf{F}_4 (\ell) = \mathsf{G}_4 (\ell)$.

nodes.name: Intersections of the F events
nodes.statement:
We denote their intersections as
\[
\mathsf{F}_k (\ell) = \cap_{i<j} \mathsf{F}_k^{i,j} (\ell), \,\, 1 \leq k \leq 3; \quad \mathsf{F}_k = \cap_{\ell \geq 1} \mathsf{F}_k (\ell), \,\, 1 \leq k \leq 4; \quad \text{and} \quad \mathsf{F} = \cap_{k=1}^4 \mathsf{F}_k.
\]

nodes.name: F(ell) is a sub-event of G(ell)
nodes.statement: For each $\ell \geq 1$, $\mathsf{F} (\ell) \subseteq \mathsf{G} (\ell)$.
nodes.label: h sub g

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Fix $\ell \geq 1$ and let $s \in [t_{\ell-1}, t_\ell]$. When $\mathsf{F}_4 (\ell) = \mathsf{G}_4 (\ell)$ occurs, $\xi_{N(s)+1} - \xi_{N(s)}$ is at most $\kappa_\ell$. In this case, Lemma~\ref{amlg2} implies that $\mathrm{dist}( \mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j ) \geq \|S_{N(s)}^{i,j}\| - 6 \kappa_\ell^2$ for every pair of distinct clusters $i < j$. This bound implies the following inclusions. First, $\mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell) \subseteq \mathsf{G}_1^{i,j} (\ell)$ holds because \begin{align*} \mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} &= \left\{ \exists s \in (t_{\ell-1},t_\ell]: \| S_{N(s)}^{i,j} \| \geq 2^\ell \epsilon_\ell^{-1} a + 6 \kappa_\ell^2 \right\}\\ &\subseteq \left\{ \exists s \in (t_{\ell-1},t_\ell]: \mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{V}_s^i,\mathcal{V}_s^j) \geq 2^\ell \epsilon_\ell^{-1} a \right\} = \mathsf{G}_1^{i,j}. \end{align*} Second, the inclusion $\mathsf{F}_2^{i,j} (\ell) \subseteq \mathsf{G}_2^{i,j}$ is justified by \begin{align*} \mathsf{F}_2^{i,j} (\ell) &\subseteq \left\{\|S_{N(s)}^{i,j}\| \geq 2^{\ell-1} \epsilon_\ell a + 6 \kappa_\ell^2, \,\, s \in [t_{\ell-1},t_\ell]\right\}\\ &\subseteq \left\{ \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j) \geq 2^{\ell-1}\epsilon_\ell a, \,\, s \in [t_{\ell-1},t_\ell] \right\} = \mathsf{G}_2^{i,j} (\ell). \end{align*} Third, $\mathsf{F}_3^{i,j} (\ell) \subseteq \mathsf{G}_3^{i,j} (\ell)$ holds because the reasoning that led to the first inclusion also shows that $\rho_\ell^{i,j} \leq N(\sigma_\ell^{i,j})$, hence \begin{align*} \mathsf{F}_3^{i,j} (\ell) &=\left\{ \|S_{m}^{i,j}\| \geq 2^\ell a + 6 \kappa_\ell^2, \,\, m \in [\rho_\ell^{i,j}, N(t_\ell)+1] \right\}\\ &\subseteq \left\{ \|S_{N(s)}^{i,j}\| \geq 2^\ell a + 6 \kappa_\ell^2, \,\, s \in [\sigma_\ell^{i,j}, t_\ell] \right\}\\ & \subseteq \left\{ \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j) \geq 2^\ell a, \,\, s \in [\sigma_\ell^{i,j}, t_\ell] \right\} = \mathsf{G}_3^{i,j} (\ell). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use Lemma 8.1 under F_4 to convert random-walk norm events into cluster distance events.

nodes.statement: Fix $\ell \geq 1$ and let $s \in [t_{\ell-1}, t_\ell]$. When $\mathsf{F}_4 (\ell) = \mathsf{G}_4 (\ell)$ occurs, $\xi_{N(s)+1} - \xi_{N(s)}$ is at most $\kappa_\ell$. In this case, Lemma~\ref{amlg2} implies that $\mathrm{dist}( \mathcal{V}_s^i, \mathcal{V}_s^j ) \geq \|S_{N(s)}^{i,j}\| - 6 \kappa_\ell^2$ for every pair of distinct clusters $i < j$. This bound implies the following inclusions.

nodes.name: Reference-time gaps stay small
nodes.statement: There exists $\alpha > 0$ such that, if $\mathcal{C}_0 \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ satisfies $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) \geq \alpha$, then \[ \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} ( \mathsf{F}_4 (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} ) \leq (8n \ell)^{-2}, \quad \ell \geq 1. \]
nodes.label: notrunc

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) = a$ for some $a > 0$. Since $N(t_\ell)$ is at most $t_\ell$, $\mathsf{F}_4 (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}}$ is a union of at most $t_\ell$ events of the form $\{\xi_m - \xi_{m-1} > \kappa_\ell\}$. Lemma~\ref{xi tail} states that there is a constant $\gamma_1 > 0$ such that \[ \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{D}_0} (\xi_m - \xi_{m-1} > s) \leq 2e^{-\gamma_1 s}, \quad s \geq 0, \] holds uniformly over $\mathcal{D}_0 \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}^\times$ that satisfy the same hypothesis as $\mathcal{C}_0$. We combine this tail bound with a union bound and the fact that $\kappa_\ell = \beta \log ( n \ell t_\ell)$: \[ \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} ( \mathsf{F}_4 (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} ) \leq 2t_\ell e^{-\gamma_1 \kappa_\ell} = \frac{2 t_\ell}{(n\ell t_\ell)^{\gamma_1 \beta}}. \] If $a$ is at least a sufficiently large constant $\alpha > 0$, simply to ensure that $t_\ell (a) \geq 1$, then a suitable choice of $\beta$ in terms of $\gamma_1$ implies the claimed bound.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over at most t_ell reference gaps with the exponential tail of Lemma 8.2.

nodes.name: F_4^c is a union of at most t_ell gap events
nodes.statement:
Assume that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) = a$ for some $a > 0$. 
Since $N(t_\ell)$ is at most $t_\ell$, $\mathsf{F}_4 (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}}$ is a union of at most $t_\ell$ events of the form $\{\xi_m - \xi_{m-1} > \kappa_\ell\}$.
nodes.statement_short: F_4^c is a union of at most t_ell gap events

nodes.name: Exponential gap tail from Lemma 8.2
nodes.statement:
Lemma~\ref{xi tail} states that there is a constant $\gamma_1 > 0$ such that 
\[
\mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{D}_0} (\xi_m - \xi_{m-1} > s) \leq 2e^{-\gamma_1 s}, \quad s \geq 0,
\] 
holds uniformly over $\mathcal{D}_0 \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}^\times$ that satisfy the same hypothesis as $\mathcal{C}_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential gap tail from Lemma 8.2

nodes.name: Union bound
nodes.statement:
We combine this tail bound with a union bound and the fact that $\kappa_\ell = \beta \log ( n \ell t_\ell)$:
\[
\mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} ( \mathsf{F}_4 (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} ) \leq 2t_\ell e^{-\gamma_1 \kappa_\ell} = \frac{2 t_\ell}{(n\ell t_\ell)^{\gamma_1 \beta}}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Union bound

nodes.name: Choose beta
nodes.statement: If $a$ is at least a sufficiently large constant $\alpha > 0$, simply to ensure that $t_\ell (a) \geq 1$, then a suitable choice of $\beta$ in terms of $\gamma_1$ implies the claimed bound.

nodes.name: Associated random walk escapes the ball in time
nodes.statement: There exists $\alpha = \alpha (d,n)$ such that, if $\mathcal{C}_0 \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ satisfies $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) \geq \alpha$, then \begin{equation} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \big( \mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \cap \mathsf{F}_4 (\ell) \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \big) \leq (8 n \ell)^{-2}, \quad \ell \geq 1, \end{equation} where $\eta_{\ell-1}$ denotes $\xi_{N(t_{\ell-1})+1}$.
nodes.label: t before n

nodes.name: Equation (9.4)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \big( \mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \cap \mathsf{F}_4 (\ell) \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \big) \leq (8 n \ell)^{-2}, \quad \ell \geq 1,
nodes.label: t bef n eq

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) = a$ for some $a > 0$. Denote $r = 2^\ell \epsilon_\ell^{-1} a + 6 \kappa_\ell^2$. By definition, \[ \mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} = \left\{ S_{m}^{i,j} \in B(r), \,\, N(t_{\ell-1}) < m \leq N(t_{\ell}) \right\}. \] Assume for the moment that, when $\mathsf{F}_4 (\ell)$ occurs, the number of steps in $\mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}}$ satisfies \begin{equation} N(t_\ell) - N(t_{\ell-1}) - 1 \geq \lambda r^2 \end{equation} with $\lambda = \gamma_3^{-1} \log \big(\gamma_2 (8 n \ell)^2 \big)$. We use \eqref{f4 claim} to prove \eqref{t bef n eq} as \begin{align*} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \cap \mathsf{F}_4 (\ell) \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) &\leq \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( S_{N(t_{\ell-1}) + 1 + m}^{i,j} \in B(r), \,\, 0 \leq m \leq \lambda r^2 \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right)\\ &= \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}}} \left( T^{i,j}_{B(r)^{\mathsf{c}}} > \lambda r^2 \right) \leq \gamma_2 e^{-\gamma_3 \lambda} = (8n\ell)^{-2}. \end{align*} The first inequality follows from the definition of $\mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}}$ and the claimed bound on $N(t_\ell)-N(t_{\ell-1})-1$; the first equality is due to the strong Markov property at time $\eta_{\ell-1}$; the second inequality holds by \eqref{esc time}, which applies because $\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$; and the second equality holds by the choice of $\lambda$. The claimed bound \eqref{f4 claim} holds when $a$ is sufficiently large. Indeed, when $\mathsf{F}_4 (\ell)$ occurs, \[ N(t_\ell) - N(t_{\ell-1}) -1 \gtrsim \kappa_\ell^{-1} (t_\ell - t_{\ell-1}). \] When $a$ is sufficiently large, this lower bound is at least $(2\kappa_\ell)^{-1} t_\ell$. It therefore suffices to show that \[ (2\kappa_\ell)^{-1} t_\ell \geq \lambda r^2. \] Some algebra shows that $(2\kappa_\ell)^{-1} t_\ell \gtrsim_n (\log a) \lambda r^2$. Consequently, there exists $\alpha = \alpha(\gamma_2,\gamma_3,n) = \alpha (d,n) > 0$ such that, if $a \geq \alpha$, then the preceding bound is satisfied.
nodes.statement_short: Show enough walk steps occur under F_4, then apply the exit-time estimate (8.5).

nodes.name: Introduce r and rewrite F_1^c
nodes.statement:
Assume that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) = a$ for some $a > 0$. Denote $r = 2^\ell \epsilon_\ell^{-1} a + 6 \kappa_\ell^2$. By definition,
\[
\mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} = \left\{ S_{m}^{i,j} \in B(r), \,\, N(t_{\ell-1}) < m \leq N(t_{\ell}) \right\}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Introduce r and rewrite F_1^c

nodes.name: Assume enough walk steps occur (9.5)
nodes.statement:
Assume for the moment that, when $\mathsf{F}_4 (\ell)$ occurs, the number of steps in $\mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}}$ satisfies
\begin{equation} N(t_\ell) - N(t_{\ell-1}) - 1 \geq \lambda r^2
\end{equation}
with $\lambda = \gamma_3^{-1} \log \big(\gamma_2 (8 n \ell)^2 \big)$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume enough walk steps occur (9.5)

nodes.name: Equation (9.5)
nodes.statement: N(t_\ell) - N(t_{\ell-1}) - 1 \geq \lambda r^2
nodes.label: f4 claim

nodes.name: Apply the exit-time estimate (8.5)
nodes.statement_short: Apply the exit-time estimate (8.5)

nodes.name: Steps between t_{ell-1} and t_ell under F_4
nodes.statement:
The claimed bound \eqref{f4 claim} holds when $a$ is sufficiently large. Indeed, when $\mathsf{F}_4 (\ell)$ occurs, 
\[
N(t_\ell) - N(t_{\ell-1}) -1 \gtrsim \kappa_\ell^{-1} (t_\ell - t_{\ell-1}).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Steps between t_{ell-1} and t_ell under F_4

nodes.name: Reduce to an inequality in a
nodes.statement:
When $a$ is sufficiently large, this lower bound is at least $(2\kappa_\ell)^{-1} t_\ell$. It therefore suffices to show that
\[
(2\kappa_\ell)^{-1} t_\ell \geq \lambda r^2.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to an inequality in a

nodes.name: Choose alpha
nodes.statement: Some algebra shows that $(2\kappa_\ell)^{-1} t_\ell \gtrsim_n (\log a) \lambda r^2$. Consequently, there exists $\alpha = \alpha(\gamma_2,\gamma_3,n) = \alpha (d,n) > 0$ such that, if $a \geq \alpha$, then the preceding bound is satisfied.
nodes.statement_short: Choose alpha

nodes.name: Separation does not drop by a factor epsilon_ell
nodes.statement: There exists $\alpha = \alpha (d,n)$ such that, if $\mathcal{C}_0 \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ satisfies $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) \geq \alpha$, then \begin{equation*} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \big( \mathsf{F}_2^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \big) \mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{G} (\ell-1)} \leq (8n\ell)^{-2}, \quad \ell \geq 1, \end{equation*} where $\eta_{\ell-1}$ denotes $\xi_{N(t_{\ell-1})+1}$.
nodes.label: h3

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) = a $ for some $a > 0$. Denote $r = 2^\ell \epsilon_\ell a + 6 \kappa_\ell^2$. By definition, \[ \mathsf{F}_2^{i,j} (\ell) = \left\{S_m^{i,j} \in B(r)^{\mathsf{c}}, \,\, N(t_{\ell-1}) \leq m \leq N (t_\ell) \right\}. \] For $\mathsf{F}_2^{i,j} (\ell)$ to occur, it suffices for the random walk from $S^{i,j}_{N(t_{\ell-1})}$ to never hit $B(r)$. In fact, when $\mathsf{G} (\ell-1)$ occurs, $S^{i,j}_{N(t_{\ell-1})} \in B(r)^{\mathsf{c}}$, so we can consider the random walk from $X = S^{i,j}_{N(t_{\ell-1})+1}$ instead. This is a minor point, so we discuss it at the end of the proof. For now, we simply use the inclusion \begin{equation} F_2^{i,j} (\ell) \cap \mathsf{G}(\ell-1) \supseteq \left\{ S_m^{i,j} \in B(r)^{\mathsf{c}}, \,m > N(t_{\ell-1})\right\} \cap \mathsf{G}(\ell-1). \end{equation} By \eqref{f2 incl}, the strong Markov property at $\eta_{\ell-1}$, and \eqref{avoid}, when $\mathsf{G} (\ell-1)$ occurs, \begin{align} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{F}_2^{i,j} (\ell) \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) &\geq \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( S_m^{i,j} \in B(r)^{\mathsf{c}}, \,m > N(t_{\ell-1}) \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) \nonumber\\ &= \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}}} \left( T_{B(r)^{\mathsf{c}}}^{i,j} = \infty \right) \geq 1 - \gamma_5 \Big( \frac{r}{\|X\|} \Big)^{d-2}. \end{align} Our use of \eqref{avoid} relies on the fact that $\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ and requies that we take $a$ sufficiently large to ensure that $r \geq \gamma_4$. To bound below $\|X\|$, we note that the separation of $\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}}$ is at least $2^{\ell-1} a$, while the diameters of the clusters are at most $2$, when $\mathsf{G} (\ell-1)$ occurs. By \eqref{tri app both}, \begin{equation} \| X \| \geq \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}}^i,\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}}^j) - \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}}^i) - \mathrm{diam} (\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}}^j) \geq 2^{\ell-1} a - 4. \end{equation} Call this lower bound $R$, in which case \eqref{h3 bd} and \eqref{f2 x bd} imply that \[ \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{F}_2^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) \mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{G}(\ell-1)} \leq \gamma_5 \Big( \frac{r}{R} \Big)^{d-2}. \] Some algebra shows that $\frac{r}{R} \gtrsim (n \ell \log a)^{-1}$ when $a$ is sufficiently large in terms of $n$. Hence, there exists $\alpha = \alpha (\gamma_4,\gamma_5,n) = \alpha (d,n) > 0$ such that, if $a \geq \alpha$, then the preceding bound is at most $(8n\ell)^{-2}$. To conclude, we explain why $S^{i,j}_{N(t_{\ell-1})} \notin B(r)$, which justifies the inclusion \eqref{f2 incl}. By \eqref{tri app both} and \eqref{xi diam bd}, and when $\mathsf{G} (\ell-1)$ occurs, \[ \| S_{N(t_{\ell-1})}^{i,j} \| \geq \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_{t_{\ell-1}}^i, \mathcal{V}_{t_{\ell-1}}^j) - 2 \left(\xi_{N(t_{\ell-1})+1} - \xi_{N(t_{\ell-1})} + 2\right) \geq 2^{\ell-1}a - 2 \kappa_{\ell-1}. \] This quantity is roughly larger than $r$ by a factor of $\ell \log a$, so $2^{\ell-1}a - 2\kappa_{\ell-1} - r > 0$ when $a$ is sufficiently large in terms of $n$. We can assume that this is true of every $a \geq \alpha$ by increasing $\alpha$ as necessary.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the avoidance estimate (8.6) from the walk's position at stage ell-1, whose norm is bounded below on G(ell-1).

nodes.name: Choose alpha so the bound is (8n ell)^{-2}
nodes.statement:
Call this lower bound $R$, in which case \eqref{h3 bd} and \eqref{f2 x bd} imply that
\[
\mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{F}_2^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) \mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{G}(\ell-1)}
\leq \gamma_5 \Big( \frac{r}{R} \Big)^{d-2}.
\]
Some algebra shows that $\frac{r}{R} \gtrsim (n \ell \log a)^{-1}$ when $a$ is sufficiently large in terms of $n$. Hence, there exists $\alpha = \alpha (\gamma_4,\gamma_5,n) = \alpha (d,n) > 0$ such that, if $a \geq \alpha$, then the preceding bound is at most $(8n\ell)^{-2}$.

nodes.name: Justify the inclusion (9.6)
nodes.statement:
To conclude, we explain why $S^{i,j}_{N(t_{\ell-1})} \notin B(r)$, which justifies the inclusion \eqref{f2 incl}. By \eqref{tri app both} and \eqref{xi diam bd}, and when $\mathsf{G} (\ell-1)$ occurs,
\[
\| S_{N(t_{\ell-1})}^{i,j} \| \geq \mathrm{dist} (\mathcal{V}_{t_{\ell-1}}^i, \mathcal{V}_{t_{\ell-1}}^j) - 2 \left(\xi_{N(t_{\ell-1})+1} - \xi_{N(t_{\ell-1})} + 2\right) \geq 2^{\ell-1}a - 2 \kappa_{\ell-1}.
\]
This quantity is roughly larger than $r$ by a factor of $\ell \log a$, so $2^{\ell-1}a - 2\kappa_{\ell-1} - r > 0$ when $a$ is sufficiently large in terms of $n$. We can assume that this is true of every $a \geq \alpha$ by increasing $\alpha$ as necessary.
nodes.statement_short: Justify the inclusion (9.6)

nodes.name: Separation stays doubled after it doubles
nodes.statement: There exists $\alpha = \alpha (d,n)$ such that, if $\mathcal{C}_0 \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ satisfies $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) \geq \alpha$, then \begin{equation*} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \big( \mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell) \cap \mathsf{F}_3^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \big) \leq (8n\ell)^{-2}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: h4

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) = a$ for some $a > 0$. When $\mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell)$ occurs, there is a first step $m \in (N (t_{\ell-1}), N (t_\ell)]$ at which $Y = S_m^{i,j}$ belongs to $B(R)^{\mathsf{c}}$, where $R = 2^\ell \epsilon_\ell^{-1} a + 6\kappa_\ell^2$. For $\mathsf{F}_3^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}}$ to occur, $S_m^{i,j}$ must hit $B(r)$, where $r = 2^\ell a + 6\kappa_\ell^2$, starting from $Y$. Note that $R$ is larger than $r$ by a factor of roughly $n \ell \log a$. By the strong Markov property at time $\xi_m$ and \eqref{avoid}, \begin{align*} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \big( \mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell) \cap \mathsf{F}_3^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \big) &= \mathbf{E}_{\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}}} \Big[ \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{V}_{\xi_m}} \big( \mathsf{F}_3^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \big); \mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell) \Big] \\ &\leq \mathbf{E}_{\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}}} \Big[ \gamma_5 \Big( \frac{r}{\| Y \|} \Big)^{d-2} \Big] \leq \gamma_5 \Big( \frac{r}{R} \Big)^{d-2}. \end{align*} Note that our use of \eqref{avoid} makes use of the fact that $\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ and, to use it, we must take $a$ sufficiently large to ensure that $r \geq \gamma_4$. Some algebra shows that $\frac{r}{R} \gtrsim (n\ell \log a)^{-1}$ when $a$ is sufficiently large. Hence, there exists $\alpha = \alpha (\gamma_4,\gamma_5,n) = \alpha (d,n) > 0$ such that, if $a \geq \alpha$, then the preceding bound is at most $(8n\ell)^{-2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Strong Markov property at the first exit from B(R) and the avoidance estimate (8.6).

nodes.name: First exit step m from B(R)
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) = a$ for some $a > 0$. When $\mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell)$ occurs, there is a first step $m \in (N (t_{\ell-1}), N (t_\ell)]$ at which $Y = S_m^{i,j}$ belongs to $B(R)^{\mathsf{c}}$, where $R = 2^\ell \epsilon_\ell^{-1} a + 6\kappa_\ell^2$.
nodes.statement_short: First exit step m from B(R)

nodes.name: F_3^c requires hitting B(r) from outside B(R)
nodes.statement: For $\mathsf{F}_3^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}}$ to occur, $S_m^{i,j}$ must hit $B(r)$, where $r = 2^\ell a + 6\kappa_\ell^2$, starting from $Y$. Note that $R$ is larger than $r$ by a factor of roughly $n \ell \log a$.
nodes.statement_short: F_3^c requires hitting B(r) from outside B(R)

nodes.name: Avoidance estimate (8.6)
nodes.statement_short: Avoidance estimate (8.6)

nodes.name: Choose alpha
nodes.statement:
Note that our use of \eqref{avoid} makes use of the fact that $\mathcal{V}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ and, to use it, we must take $a$ sufficiently large to ensure that $r \geq \gamma_4$. 
Some algebra shows that $\frac{r}{R} \gtrsim (n\ell \log a)^{-1}$ when $a$ is sufficiently large. Hence, there exists $\alpha = \alpha (\gamma_4,\gamma_5,n) = \alpha (d,n) > 0$ such that, if $a \geq \alpha$, then the preceding bound is at most $(8n\ell)^{-2}$.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha$ be the largest of the constants it names in Propositions~\ref{notrunc} through \ref{h4}, and assume that $\mathcal{C}_0 \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ satisfies $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) \geq \alpha$. We aim to show that \begin{equation} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{G} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \mid \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) \mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{G} (\ell-1)} \leq (8 \ell)^{-2}, \end{equation} in terms of $\eta_{\ell-1} = \xi_{N(t_{\ell-1})+1}$. By Proposition~\ref{h sub g} and a union bound over distinct pairs of clusters, we have \begin{equation} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{G} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \mid \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) \leq \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{F} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \mid \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) \leq \sum_{i < j} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{F}^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \mid \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right). \end{equation} Using the fact that, for events $E_1$ and $E_2$, $E_2^{\mathsf{c}}$ is contained in the disjoint union $( E_1 \cap E_2^{\mathsf{c}} ) \cup E_1^{\mathsf{c}}$, we find that \begin{multline*} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{F}^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) \leq 3 \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{F}_4 (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) + 2 \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \cap \mathsf{F}_4 (\ell) \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right)\\ + \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{F}_2^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) + \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{F}_1^{i,j} (\ell) \cap \mathsf{F}_3^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \bigm\vert \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right). \end{multline*} When $\mathsf{G}(\ell-1)$ occurs, we can apply Propositions~\ref{notrunc} through \ref{h4} to bound the terms on the right-hand side as \[ \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \big( \mathsf{F}^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \mid \mathscr{F}_{t_{\ell-1}} \big) \mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{G}(\ell-1)} \leq 8(n\ell)^{-2}. \] The bound \eqref{loc qg1} then follows from \eqref{g to h} and the fact that there are at most $n^2$ distinct pairs of clusters.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over pairs and over the four failure modes, then Propositions 9.4-9.8.

Let $\alpha$ be the largest of the constants it names in Propositions~\ref{notrunc} through \ref{h4}, and assume that $\mathcal{C}_0 \in \mathrm{Ref}^\times$ satisfies $\mathrm{sep} (\mathcal{C}_0) \geq \alpha$. We aim to show that 
\begin{equation} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \left( \mathsf{G} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \mid \mathscr{F}_{\eta_{\ell-1}} \right) \mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{G} (\ell-1)} \leq (8 \ell)^{-2},
\end{equation}
in terms of $\eta_{\ell-1} = \xi_{N(t_{\ell-1})+1}$.

\mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{C}_0} \big( \mathsf{F}^{i,j} (\ell)^{\mathsf{c}} \mid \mathscr{F}_{t_{\ell-1}} \big) \mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{G}(\ell-1)} \leq 8(n\ell)^{-2}.

nodes.name: Two-stage procedure (diameter-dependent)
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange V into a segment, then treadmill pairs off its tip one at a time; the first stage may cost a diameter-dependent probability.
nodes.section: 10 Strategy for the proof of Theorem 5

nodes.name: Rearrange V into a segment in the -e_1 direction
nodes.statement: First, we rearrange $V$ into a line segment emanating in the $-e_1$ direction from, say, the element of $V$ which is least in the lexicographic ordering of $\mathbb{Z}^d$.
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange V into a segment in the -e_1 direction
nodes.section: 10 Strategy for the proof of Theorem 5

nodes.name: Treadmill pairs off the tip until two or three remain
nodes.statement: Second, we ``treadmill'' (Figures~\ref{treadmill} and \ref{treadmill2}) a pair of elements from the ``tip'' of the segment, in the $-e_1$ direction, until the pair is sufficiently far from the other elements. We then repeat this process, one pair at a time, until only two or three elements of the initial segment remain.
nodes.statement_short: Treadmill pairs off the tip until two or three remain
nodes.section: 10 Strategy for the proof of Theorem 5

nodes.name: Lined-up
nodes.statement: We say that $\mathcal{C} \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}^\times$ can be lined-up with separation $r > 0$ if $\mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{C}^i, \mathcal{C}^{\neq i}) \geq 2r$ and if $\mathcal{C}^i$ is a connected subset of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, for every $1 \leq i \leq \#\mathcal{C}$. We also say that the union $\cup_i \mathcal{C}^i \in \mathrm{Conf}_{d,n}$ can be lined-up with separation $r$.
nodes.section: 10 Strategy for the proof of Theorem 5
nodes.label: def lined up

nodes.name: Lex element
nodes.statement: We say that an element $x$ of a finite set $A \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ is lex in $A$, denoted $\mathrm{lex} (A) = x$, if it is least among the elements of $A$ in the lexicographic order of $\mathbb{Z}^d$.
nodes.section: 10 Strategy for the proof of Theorem 5
differentia: least among the elements of $A$ in the lexicographic order of $\mathbb{Z}^d$

nodes.name: Three-stage procedure for forming DOTs
nodes.statement_short: Algorithm 1 forms separated connected clumps, Algorithm 2 lines each clump up into a segment, Algorithm 3 treadmills pairs off into a DOT clustering.
nodes.section: 10 Strategy for the proof of Theorem 5

nodes.name: Algorithm 1: separated connected clumps
nodes.statement: First, we will use Algorithm $\mathcal{A}_{\ref{alg1}}$ to construct a clustering $\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{A}_{\ref{alg1}} (V,a)$ of a configuration which can be lined-up with separation $dn^2 a$. This algorithm is the most complicated of the three. In brief, the algorithm repeatedly attempts to create a non-isolated lex element of a cluster, so that it can be ``treadmilled'' in the $-e_1$ direction---along with a neighboring element---to form a new dimer cluster.
nodes.statement_short: Algorithm 1: separated connected clumps
nodes.section: 10 Strategy for the proof of Theorem 5

nodes.name: Algorithm 2: line up each clump
nodes.statement:
In the second stage, we will apply Algorithm $\mathcal{A}_{\ref{alg2}}$ to ``line-up'' the elements of each cluster $\mathcal{C}^i$. Specifically, in terms of the line segment
\begin{equation} L_k = \big\{ -j e_1: j \in \{0,1,\dots,k-1\} \big\}, \quad k \geq 1,
\end{equation}
we will rearrange the elements of $\mathcal{C}^i$ into the set $\mathrm{lex} (\mathcal{C}^i) + L_{|\mathcal{C}^i|}$. Specifically, the resulting clustering will be
\[ \mathcal{A}_{\ref{alg2}} (\mathcal{C}) = \left( \mathrm{lex} (\mathcal{C}^i) + L_{|\mathcal{C}^i|} \right)_{i=1}^{\# \mathcal{C}}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Algorithm 2: line up each clump
nodes.section: 10 Strategy for the proof of Theorem 5

nodes.name: Equation (10.1)
nodes.statement: L_k = \big\{ -j e_1: j \in \{0,1,\dots,k-1\} \big\}, \quad k \geq 1,
nodes.section: 10 Strategy for the proof of Theorem 5
nodes.label: line segment

nodes.name: Algorithm 3: treadmill pairs into DOTs
nodes.statement: In the third stage, Algorithm $\mathcal{A}_{\ref{alg3}}$ will iteratively treadmill pairs of elements from each segment in the $-e_1$ direction for multiples of $a$ steps until only a dimer or a trimer of the original segment remains (Figure~\ref{treadmill2}). The resulting clustering $\mathcal{A} (V,a) = \mathcal{A}_{\ref{alg3}} (\mathcal{A}_{\ref{alg2}} (\mathcal{C}), a)$ will be an $(a,1)$ DOT clustering.
nodes.statement_short: Algorithm 3: treadmill pairs into DOTs
nodes.section: 10 Strategy for the proof of Theorem 5

nodes.name: Short paths between points of the visible boundary
nodes.statement: Let $d \geq 1$. Let $A$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ that contains the origin, and let $x$ and $y$ be distinct elements of $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} A$. There is a path $\Gamma$ from $x$ to $y$ in $A^{\mathsf{c}}$ of length at most $\sqrt{d} \, \mathrm{diam} (A) + 3^{d+1} |A|$. Moreover, $\Gamma$ is contained in $\{z \in \mathbb{Z}^d: \|z\| \leq \mathrm{diam} (A) + \sqrt{d}\}$.
assumptions: Let $A$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ that contains the origin, and let $x$ and $y$ be distinct elements of $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} A$
conclusions: There is a path $\Gamma$ from $x$ to $y$ in $A^{\mathsf{c}}$ of length at most $\sqrt{d} \, \mathrm{diam} (A) + 3^{d+1} |A|$

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Fix a finite set $A \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ containing the origin, and fix two elements, $x$ and $y$, in $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} A$. Let $\{B_i\}_i$ be the collection of $\ast$-connected components of $A$. Because $A$ is finite, each $B_i$ is finite and, as each $B_i$ is also $\ast$-connected, each $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} B_i$ is connected in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by Lemma~\ref{kesten result}. If $\Gamma$ is the path of least length from $x$ to $y$, then this length, denoted $|\Gamma|$, satisfies \[ |\Gamma| \leq \sqrt{d} \mathrm{diam} (A) + 2d. \] Indeed, by definition, if $u \in \partial_{\mathrm{vis}} A$, then there is $v \in A$ such that $\|u-v\| \leq \sqrt{d}$. By the triangle inequality, $\mathrm{diam} (\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} A)$ is at most $\mathrm{diam} (A) + 2\sqrt{d}$, which implies the bound on $|\Gamma|$ because $|\Gamma| \leq \sqrt{d}\|x-y\|$. We will edit $\Gamma$ to obtain a potentially longer path which does not intersect $A$. If $\Gamma$ does not intersect $A$, then we are done. Otherwise, let $i_1$ denote the label of the first $\ast$-connected component of $A$ intersected by $\Gamma$. Additionally, denote by $u$ and $v$ the first and last indices of $\Gamma$ which intersect $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} B_{i_1}$. Because $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} B_{i_1}$ is connected in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, there is a path $\Lambda$ in $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} B_{i_1}$ from $\Gamma_u$ to $\Gamma_v$. We may therefore edit $\Gamma$ to form $\Gamma'$: \[ \Gamma' = \big( \Gamma_1, \dots, \Gamma_{u-1}, \Lambda_1, \dots, \Lambda_{|\Lambda|}, \Gamma_{v+1}, \dots, \Gamma_{|\Gamma|} \big). \] If $\Gamma'$ does not intersect $A$, then we are done, as $\Gamma'$ is contained in the union of $\Gamma$ and $\cup_i \partial_{\mathrm{vis}} B_i$, and because $\cup_i \partial_{\mathrm{vis}} B_i$ has at most $3^d |A|$ elements. Accordingly, \begin{equation} |\Gamma'| \leq \sqrt{d} \mathrm{diam} (A) + 2d + 3^d |A| \leq \sqrt{d}\, \mathrm{diam} (A) + 3^{d+1} |A|. \end{equation} Otherwise, if $\Gamma'$ intersects another $\ast$-connected component $B_{i_2}$ of $A$, we can argue in an analogous fashion to obtain a path $\Gamma''$ which intersects neither $B_{i_1}$ nor $B_{i_2}$. Like $\Gamma'$, $\Gamma''$ is contained in the union of $\Gamma$ and $\cup_i \partial_{\mathrm{vis}} B_i$ and so its length satisfies the same upper bound. By continuing inductively, we obtain a path from $x$ to $y$ with a length of at most the right-hand side of \eqref{gam length}. The path is contained in the union of $\Gamma$ and $\cup_i \partial_{\mathrm{vis}} B_i$, which is contained in $\{z \in \mathbb{Z}^d: \|z\| \leq \mathrm{diam} (A) + \sqrt{d}\}$ because $A$ contains the origin by assumption.
nodes.statement_short: Take a shortest path and reroute it around each *-connected component along its connected visible boundary.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $x, y$ be elements of $A$ which are exposed in $A \cup B$. If $u$ is any element of $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} A \cap \partial \{x\}$ and $v$ is any element of $\partial_{\mathrm{vis}} A \cap \partial \{y\}$, then, by Lemma \ref{kesten cor}, there is a path $\Gamma$ from $u$ to $v$ in $A^{\mathsf{c}}$ of length at most \[ \sqrt{d} \, \mathrm{diam} (A) + 3^{d+1} |A| \leq 1.1 \cdot 3^{d+1} n \leq 4^d n.\] The first inequality is due to the assumption that $A$ is connected, which implies that $\mathrm{diam} (A)$ is at most $n$, and the fact that $\sqrt{d} \leq 0.1 \cdot 3^{d+1}$ when $d \geq 5$. The second inequality holds because $d \geq 5$. Because $B$ is a distance of at least $4^d n$ from $A$, $\Gamma$ must also lie outside of $B$. This implies that there is a constant $c = c(d,n)$ such that \[ \mathrm{esc}_{A \cup B} (x) \geq c \mathrm{esc}_{A \cup B} (y).\] Dividing by the capacity of $A \cup B$ gives \eqref{hm comp}.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Suppose that $x$ is lex in $A$ and that there are positive integers $k$ and $\ell$ for which $\mathrm{dist} (A, B) \geq 2^k \ell \sqrt{d}$. We will bound below the probability that a random walk from $x$ escapes $A \cup B$ by bounding below the probability that it (1) takes $\ell$ steps in the $-e_1$ direction, then (2) exits a sequence of doubling cubes through their $-e_1$ directed faces until it is at least a distance of $2^{k-1} \ell$ from $A \cup B$, and (3) subsequently never returns to $A \cup B$. First, a random walk from $x$ reaches $x-\ell e_1$ before returning to $A \cup B$ with a probability of at least $(2d)^{-\ell}$: \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{x-\ell e_1} < \tau_{A \cup B}) \geq (2d)^{-\ell}. \end{equation} The random walk can do so, for example, by following $(x-e_1,x-2e_1,\dots, x - \ell e_1)$, which lies outside of $A \cup B$ because $x$ is lex in $A$ and because $B$ is a distance of at least $2^k \ell \sqrt{d} > \ell$ from $x$. Second, for $u \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\ell \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, define $Q (u,\ell)$ to be the open cube centered at $u$ and with side length $2\ell$, and denote the $-e_1$ directed face of its boundary by $F(u,\ell)$: \[ Q(u,\ell) = \left\{z \in \mathbb{Z}^d: \max_{1 \leq i \leq d} |z_i - u_i| < \ell \right\} \quad \text{and} \quad F(u,\ell) = \left\{z \in \partial Q (u,\ell): z_1 = \min_{v \in \partial Q (u,\ell)} v_1 \right\}. \] We inductively define cube centers $X_j$, cubes $Q_j$, and faces $F_j$ according to $X_1 = x-\ell e_1$, \[ Q_j = Q(X_j,2^{j-1}\ell), \quad F_j = F(X_j,2^{j-1} \ell), \quad \text{and} \quad X_{j+1} = S_{\tau_{\partial Q_j}}, \quad j \geq 1. \] When $\cap_{i=2}^j \{X_i \in F_{i-1}\}$ occurs, $X_j$ satisfies \[ \mathrm{dist} (A, X_j) \geq 2^{j-1} \ell \quad \text{and} \quad \mathrm{dist}(B, X_j) \geq \mathrm{dist} (A,B) - 2^{j-1} \ell \sqrt{d}, \quad j \geq 1. \] Since the distance between $A$ and $B$ is at least $2^k \ell \sqrt{d}$, this bound implies that \[ \mathrm{dist} (A \cup B, X_k) \geq 2^{k-1} \ell. \] Hence, if $C = \{z \in \mathbb{Z}^d: \mathrm{dist}(z, A \cup B) < 2^{k-1}\ell\}$, then \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_{X_1} (\tau_{\partial C} < \tau_{A \cup B}) \geq \mathbb{P}_{X_1} (\cap_{j=2}^k \{X_j \in F_{j-1}\}) = (2d)^{-(k-1)}. \end{equation} The equality follows the strong Markov property applied to $\tau_{\partial F_{j}}$ for each $j \geq 1$ and the fact that $\mathbb{P}_{X_{j}} (X_{j+1} \in F_{j}) = (2d)^{-1}$, by symmetry. Third, when $\{\tau_{\partial C} < \tau_{A \cup B}\}$ occurs, the probability that the random walk never returns to $A \cup B$ is at least the minimum of $\mathbb{P}_z (\tau_{A \cup B} = \infty)$ over $z \in \partial C$. The distance from $\partial C$ to $A \cup B$ is at least $2^{k-1} \ell$. By Lemma~\ref{simple set hit}, there is a constant $\ell_0 = \ell_0 (d) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ such that, if $\ell \geq \ell_0$, then \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_x (\tau_{A \cup B} = \infty \mid \tau_{X_1} < \tau_{\partial C} < \tau_{A \cup B}) \geq \min_{z \in \partial C} \mathbb{P}_z \left( \tau_{A \cup B} = \infty \right) \geq 1 - n 2^{-k(d-2)}. \end{equation} Combining \eqref{lex esc bd1}, \eqref{lex esc bd2}, and \eqref{lex esc bd3}, and taking $\ell = \ell_0$, we find that \begin{equation} \mathrm{esc}_{A\cup B} (x) \gtrsim (2d)^{-k+1} (1 - n 2^{-k (d-2)}). \end{equation} If $n$ is at most $2^{d-3}$, then choosing $k=1$ in \eqref{lex esc bd} results in a constant lower bound, depending on $d$ only. Otherwise, if $n$ exceeds $2^{d-3}$, then we can take $k$ to be the integer part of $\log_2 ((2n)^{\frac{1}{d-2}})$, in which case \eqref{lex esc bd} gives \begin{equation*} \mathrm{esc}_{A \cup B} (x) \gtrsim n^{-\frac{1+ \log_2 (d)}{d-2}}. \end{equation*} Because $\mathrm{cap} (A \cup B)$ is at most $n G(o)^{-1}$, the preceding bound implies that \begin{equation*} \mathbb{H}_{A \cup B} (x) \gtrsim n^{-\frac{d-1 + \log_2 (d)}{d-2}}. \end{equation*} We conclude the proof by setting $r = 2^{k_0}\ell_0 \sqrt{d}$, where $k_0$ is the larger of $1$ and the integer part of $\log_2 ((2n)^{\frac{1}{d-2}})$.
